analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates current strategies for preventing and treating HPV-associated precancerous lesions, focusing on high-risk HPV types (primarily HPV16 and HPV18). It synthesizes evidence on viral oncogene mechanisms, diagnostic biomarkers (p16/Ki-67, DNA methylation, microRNAs), and evolving therapeutic approaches, including fertility-sparing alternatives to standard surgical excision. Non-invasive modalities such as thermal ablation, photodynamic therapy, and imiquimod demonstrate high lesion regression and viral clearance rates while preserving cervical integrity. The authors argue that management is shifting toward personalized, molecularly guided paradigms. The review emphasizes expanding global vaccine access and implementing multi-modal, minimally invasive strategies to address the persistent burden of HPV-associated disease, particularly in low- and middle-income countries.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)感染是宫颈癌及其前驱病变的主要原因,尽管疫苗接种和筛查技术有所进展,但其仍是全球主要的健康负担。本综述旨在综合当前关于HPV病毒学、疫苗接种、诊断生物标志物以及不断演变的管理策略的知识。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是一项全面的文献综述,综合当前关于HPV主要类型(尤其是HPV16和HPV18)及其相关癌前病变的证据。它评估了诊断和治疗方法,但未具体指定某一定义的人群或研究环境。
elements_zh.methods: 本综述综合了关于HPV致癌基因机制(E6和E7)、多模式筛查方案以及治疗干预的文献,包括手术切除、热消融、光动力疗法和局部免疫调节剂如咪喹莫特。它还探讨了分子标志物(p16/Ki-67、DNA甲基化特征、循环微RNA)和针对微生物组的辅助治疗。
elements_zh.main_results: 综述指出,大环切除术(LLETZ)仍是治疗高级别宫颈上皮内瘤变(CIN)的黄金标准,但其相关的产科并发症需要采用保留生育能力的替代方案。非侵入性治疗手段如热消融、光动力疗法和咪喹莫特能够实现高病变消退率和病毒清除率,同时保持宫颈结构的完整性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为HPV相关癌前病变管理正向个性化、分子导向且保留生育能力的策略转变的证据。他们强调了先进诊断生物标志物和微创治疗的整合作为该领域的新发展。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持扩大全球疫苗接种的可及性,并实施多模式、微创的治疗策略,以减轻宫颈癌的负担,尤其是在低收入和中等收入国家。综述强调了分子诊断和保留生育能力的治疗在改善患者预后中的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据未报告具体研究设计的局限性、偏倚、混杂因素或主要数据的样本量限制。作为仅基于摘要的综述,其证据强度受限于依赖于综合文献而非原始实证数据,因此需要中等置信度评估。}}.{

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)感染是宫颈癌及其即发前体病变(统称为宫颈上皮内瘤变,CIN)的主要病因。尽管通过预防性疫苗接种和二级筛查显著降低了宫颈癌发病率,但宫颈癌仍是全球重要的公共卫生负担,尤其在中低收入国家。本综述全面评估了HPV病毒学、流行病学、先进诊断风险分层生物标志物及演变中的管理范式的当前格局。方法:本综述综合了当前文献,涵盖高危型HPV(主要为HPV16和18型)、病毒致癌机制(E6和E7)、多模式筛查方案及从标准手术切除到新兴非侵入性治疗方式的治疗干预措施。结果:尽管转化区大环切术(LLETZ)仍是高级别CIN的金标准,但其相关产科并发症要求采用保留生育功能的替代方案。近期进展凸显了非侵入性治疗方式的有效性——包括热消融、光动力疗法(PDT)及局部免疫调节剂(如咪喹莫特)——这些方法在实现高比例病变消退和病毒清除的同时,保持了宫颈结构完整性。此外,通过整合分子标志物(p16/Ki-67、DNA甲基化特征及循环微RNA)和新兴的微生物群靶向辅助治疗,诊断精度显著提升。结论:HPV相关癌前病变的管理正从标准化手术切除转向个体化、分子指导的保留生育功能范式。未来临床工作需重点扩大全球疫苗接种覆盖范围,同时实施多模式、微创治疗策略。

papers.title: Prevalence of high-risk human papillomavirus and cytological correlation in Gujarati women: implications for regional screening and vaccination strategies
papers.abstract: Abstract Background High-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infection is a major etiological factor for cervical cancer. HPV-16 and HPV-18 are the most prevalent oncogenic subtypes of cancer. Despite the availability of preventive strategies, cervical cancer remains a public health concern in India. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of hrHPV genotypes and evaluate their association with cervical cytological abnormalities among women in Gujarat, India. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 9,706 married women aged ≥ 30 years who attended community-based screening camps organized by the Gujarat Cancer Research Institute between January 2022 and December 2023. Cervical samples were collected for hrHPV DNA detection using the Roche COBAS ® 4800 platform, and liquid-based cytology was performed in hrHPV-positive cases. Statistical analysis was used to assess genotype-specific prevalence and associations with demographic and clinical variables. Results Overall, 4.9% ( n = 478) of women were hrHPV positive, with non-16/18 hrHPV types accounting for most infections (62.8%), followed by HPV-16 (18%) and HPV-18 (8.4%). Multivariate analysis revealed that early age at marriage, early age at first pregnancy, and abnormal cervical findings on examination were independently associated with hrHPV positivity, with malignant cervical findings showing the strongest association (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 38.2; 95% CI: 3.4–429.1) and early pregnancy conferring an approximately fourfold risk (adjusted OR = 4.29; 95% CI: 2.31–7.96). HPV-16 showed the strongest association with cytological abnormality, particularly high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL) (OR = 6.18; 95% CI: 3.10–12.4), and HPV-16/18 co-infection further increased the risk of HSIL (OR = 31.33). Conclusion The predominance of non-16/18 hrHPV genotypes, combined with the strong HPV-16–HSIL association, underscores the importance of extended-genotype vaccination, genotype-informed screening, and reproductive health interventions (e.g., preventing early marriage and pregnancy). These findings directly support the WHO’s cervical cancer elimination strategy and call for policy actions to expand vaccine coverage, strengthen screening, and implement context-specific prevention strategies in Gujarat.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 尽管有预防策略,宫颈癌仍然是印度的一个公共卫生问题。高危型HPV(hrHPV)感染是宫颈癌的主要病因。人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)-16和HPV-18是导致癌症的最常见致癌亚型。本研究旨在估计古吉拉特邦女性中高危型HPV基因型的患病率,并评估其与宫颈细胞学异常之间的关联。方法 本研究在2022年1月至2023年12月期间,对参加古吉拉特癌症研究所在社区组织的筛查活动的9,706名≥30岁的已婚女性进行了横断面研究。使用Roche COBAS ® 4800平台采集宫颈样本以检测hrHPV DNA,并在hrHPV阳性病例中进行液基细胞学检查。统计分析用于评估特定基因型的患病率及其与人口统计学和临床变量的关联。结果 总体而言,4.9%(n=478)的女性为hrHPV阳性,其中非16/18型hrHPV占感染的大多数(62.8%),其次是HPV-16(18%)和HPV-18(8.4%)。多变量分析显示,早婚、早孕以及体检中发现的宫颈异常与hrHPV阳性独立相关,其中恶性宫颈发现与hrHPV阳性关联最强(调整后的比值比[OR]=38.2;95% CI: 3.4–429.1),而早孕则带来约四倍的风险(调整后的OR=4.29;95% CI: 2.31–7.96)。HPV-16与细胞学异常,特别是高级别鳞状上皮内病变(HSIL)关联最强(OR=6.18;95% CI: 3.10–12.4),而HPV-16/18共感染进一步增加了HSIL的风险(OR=31.33)。结论 非16/18型高危型HPV基因型的主导地位,加上HPV-16与HSIL的强关联,突显了在古吉拉特邦实施扩展基因型监测和基于基因型的筛查策略的重要性。此外,强调了生殖健康干预措施(如防止早婚和早孕)的必要性。这些发现直接支持世界卫生组织(WHO)的宫颈癌消除策略,并呼吁采取政策行动,扩大筛查覆盖范围,加强监测,并在古吉拉特邦实施针对性的预防策略。

papers.title: Immune response and durability of human papillomavirus antibodies in vaccinated adolescents after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: a pilot study
papers.abstract: Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), preceded by chemotherapy and/or total body irradiation, eradicates hematopoietic cells, including vaccine-primed memory cells. Revaccination is therefore required after HSCT. Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is particularly important in this population because of the increased risk of HPV-associated anogenital and oropharyngeal cancers. While the World Health Organization (WHO) currently recommends a single HPV vaccine dose for immunocompetent adolescents, 3 doses are recommended for immunocompromised individuals. To evaluate the immunogenicity of HPV vaccination in adolescents following HSCT. Two cohorts were studied. Cohort 1 was a quasi-experimental study assessing seroconversion after a 2-dose schedule of HPV vaccination in post-HSCT adolescents aged 9–15 years. Eligible participants were ≥ 1 year post-HSCT and had discontinued immunosuppressive therapy for ≥ 6 months. Participants received 2-dose quadrivalent HPV (qHPV) vaccine at 0 and 6 months. Anti-HPV16 L1 IgG and anti-HPV18 L1 IgG levels were measured 6 months after the first dose and 1 month after the second dose. Cohort 2 was a cross-sectional study evaluating the persistence of anti-HPV16 and anti-HPV18 antibodies in vaccinated post-HSCT adolescents at varying intervals after completion of the vaccination series. Twenty-three participants were enrolled in Cohort 1. Six months after the first vaccine dose, the proportions who seroconverted were 54.5% for HPV 16 and 68.2% for HPV 18. One month after the second dose, the proportions who seroconverted increased to 95.5% for HPV 16 and 90.9% for HPV 18. Local adverse events occurred in 22–39% of participants within 48 h after vaccination, whereas systemic adverse events were infrequent. No serious adverse events were observed. In Cohort 2, 15 participants were included. The interval since the last vaccine dose ranged from 6 to 62 months. All participants had detectable antibodies against HPV16, and all but one had detectable antibodies against HPV18. The findings from this pilot study provide preliminary evidence that a 2-dose HPV vaccination schedule may induce a better antibody response in adolescents after HSCT; however, further studies with larger sample sizes and serial assessment of antibody titers are needed to determine the optimal dosing strategy and long-term durability of immunity.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the immunogenicity of HPV vaccination in adolescents who had undergone hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), as HSCT eradicates vaccine-primed memory cells and revaccination is required in this population.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study included two cohorts: Cohort 1 was a quasi-experimental study assessing seroconversion after a 2-dose schedule of HPV vaccination in post-HSCT adolescents aged 9–15 years, while Cohort 2 was a cross-sectional study evaluating antibody persistence in vaccinated post-HSCT adolescents at varying intervals post-vaccination. Twenty-three participants were enrolled in Cohort 1, and 15 in Cohort 2.
analysis.methods: Anti-HPV16 L1 IgG and anti-HPV18 L1 IgG levels were measured 6 months after the first dose and 1 month after the second dose in Cohort 1. In Cohort 2, antibody persistence was evaluated in participants whose vaccination series had been completed between 6 and 62 months prior.
analysis.main_results: Six months after the first vaccine dose, 54.5% of participants seroconverted for HPV 16 and 68.2% for HPV 18. One month after the second dose, these proportions increased to 95.5% for HPV 16 and 90.9% for HPV 18. In Cohort 2, all participants had detectable antibodies against HPV16, and all but one had detectable antibodies against HPV18.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that a 2-dose HPV vaccination schedule may induce a better antibody response in adolescents after HSCT, which is a novel observation in this specific immunocompromised population.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide preliminary evidence for the effectiveness of a 2-dose HPV vaccination schedule in post-HSCT adolescents, which could inform future vaccination strategies and long-term immunity monitoring in this high-risk group.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a pilot with a small sample size, and the evidence is limited to antibody levels without long-term outcome data. The confidence in these findings is moderate due to the study's design and limited scope.

analysis.summary_en: This pilot study investigated the immune response to HPV vaccination in adolescents who had undergone hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). It found that a 2-dose schedule induced seroconversion rates of 54.5% for HPV 16 and 68.2% for HPV 18 at 6 months post-first dose, increasing to 95.5% and 90.9% respectively one month after the second dose. In a cross-sectional cohort, all participants had detectable HPV16 antibodies, and all but one had HPV18 antibodies. The study suggests that a 2-dose schedule may be more effective in this population, though larger studies are needed to confirm these findings. The results have implications for optimizing HPV vaccination strategies in immunocompromised adolescents post-HSCT, but the evidence is limited by the small sample size and lack of long-term outcome data.

papers.title_zh: 免疫应答和疫苗接种后造血干细胞移植青少年人乳头瘤病毒抗体的持久性:一项试点研究
papers.source_body_en: Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), preceded by chemotherapy and/or total body irradiation, eradicates hematopoietic cells, including vaccine-primed memory cells. Revaccination is therefore required after HSCT. Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is particularly important in this population because of the increased risk of HPV-associated anogenital and oropharyngeal cancers. While the World Health Organization (WHO) currently recommends a single HPV vaccine dose for immunocompetent adolescents, 3 doses are recommended for immunocompromised individuals. To evaluate the immunogenicity of HPV vaccination in adolescents following HSCT. Two cohorts were studied. Cohort 1 was a quasi-experimental study assessing seroconversion after a 2-dose schedule of HPV vaccination in post-HSCT adolescents aged 9–15 years. Eligible participants were ≥ 1 year post-HSCT and had discontinued immunosuppressive therapy for ≥ 6 months. Participants received 2-dose quadrivalent HPV (qHPV) vaccine at 0 and 6 months. Anti-HPV16 L1 IgG and anti-HPV18 L1 IgG levels were measured 6 months after the first dose and 1 month after the second dose. Cohort 2 was a cross-sectional study evaluating the persistence of anti-HPV16 and anti-HPV18 antibodies in vaccinated post-HSCT adolescents at varying intervals after completion of the vaccination series. Twenty-three participants were enrolled in Cohort 1. Six months after the first vaccine dose, the proportions who seroconverted were 54.5% for HPV 16 and 68.2% for HPV 18. One month after the second dose, the proportions who seroconverted increased to 95.5% for HPV 16 and 90.9% for HPV 18. Local adverse events occurred in 22–39% of participants within 48 h after vaccination, whereas systemic adverse events were infrequent. No serious adverse events were observed. In Cohort 2, 15 participants were included. The interval since the last vaccine dose ranged from 6 to 62 months. All participants had detectable antibodies against HPV16, and all but one had detectable antibodies against HPV18. The findings from this pilot study provide preliminary evidence that a 2-dose HPV vaccination schedule may induce a better antibody response in adolescents after HSCT; however, further studies with larger sample sizes and serial assessment of antibody titers are needed to determine the optimal dosing strategy and long-term durability of immunity.

papers.title: Human Papillomavirus-Related Diseases in Urology: Diagnosis, Treatment, Prevention, and Clinical Considerations for Healthcare Providers
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) has long been regarded as a gynecologic pathogen, yet its disease burden in men is substantial and rapidly increasing. In Korea, the prevalence of anogenital warts in men has tripled over the past decade, penile cancer continues to rise, and HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer (OPC) incidence in men has already exceeded that of cervical cancer in comparable high-income countries. This review reframes HPV as an urgent urological, occupational, and public health concern. Drawing primarily on the 2023 Korean Sexually Transmitted Infection (STI) Guidelines and the 2021 U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention STI Treatment Guidelines, supplemented by original primary literature retrieved from PubMed, we address: (1) the male-specific epidemiological shift; (2) nonsexual and occupational transmission routes, with particular emphasis on surgical smoke; (3) evidence-based infection control in urology practice; (4) clinical management of anogenital warts; (5) male HPV vaccination policy, international comparisons, and cost-effectiveness; and (6) future research priorities including OPC prevention, HPV and male infertility, and the need for urology-specific infection control guidelines. From 2026, Korea will include 12-year-old boys in its National Immunization Program—the first gender-neutral HPV vaccination policy in Korea. This review highlights the expanding and indispensable role of urologists in HPV management and emphasizes that infection control vigilance and gender-neutral vaccination strategies are essential to reduce the mounting societal burden of HPV-related diseases. This review provides a practical framework for urologists to integrate HPV prevention, infection control, and vaccination counseling into routine clinical practice.

papers.abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 长期以来被认为是一种妇科病原体,但其在男性中的疾病负担却很大且迅速增加。在韩国,过去十年中男性肛门生殖器疣的 发病率 增加了两倍,阴茎癌持续上升,男性 HPV 阳性口咽癌 (OPC) 发病率 已经超过了可比高收入国家的 发病率。这篇综述将 HPV 重新定义为一个紧迫的泌尿科、职业和公共卫生问题。主要借鉴 2023 年韩国性传播感染 (STI) 指南和 2021 年美国疾病控制与预防中心 STI 治疗 指南,并辅以从 PubMed 检索到的原始原始文献,我们解决了:(1) 男性特异性流行病学转变;(2)非性和职业性的传播途径,特别强调手术烟雾;(3)泌尿外科实践中循证感染控制;(4)肛门生殖器疣的临床治疗;(5)男性HPV 疫苗接种政策、国际比较及成本效益;(6) 未来的研究重点,包括 OPC 预防、HPV 和男性不育,以及泌尿科特定感染控制指南的需求。从 2026 年起,韩国将把 12 岁男孩纳入国家免疫计划,这是韩国首个性别中立的 HPV 疫苗接种 政策。这篇综述强调了泌尿科医师在 HPV 管理中不断扩大且不可或缺的作用,并强调感染控制警惕和性别中立的 疫苗接种 策略对于减少 HPV 相关疾病日益增加的社会负担至关重要。本综述为泌尿科医生提供了一个实用的框架,将 HPV 预防、感染控制和 疫苗接种 咨询纳入常规临床实践。

papers.title: A comparative study of treatment of persistent cervical low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions with HPV16/18 infection.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Current treatment options for persistent cervical low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL) with HPV16/18 infection have certain limitations. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of 5-aminolevulinic acid photodynamic therapy (ALA-PDT) in these patients. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 304 outpatients with persistent cervical LSIL with HPV16/18 infection in our hospital from January 2023 to December 2024. Based on the treatment received, patients were divided into three groups: ALA-PDT group, loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP) group, and observation group. After diagnosis and corresponding treatment, patients were followed up for one year. The LSIL regression rates, HPV16/18 clearance rates, and adverse effects were compared among the three groups. RESULTS: The ALA-PDT, LEEP, and observation groups respectively enrolled 90, 42, and 172 patients. The cervical LSIL regression rates in the ALA-PDT, LEEP, and observation groups were 85.56%, 90.48%, and 56.98%, respectively. The difference between the ALA-PDT and LEEP groups was not statistically significant, but both were significantly superior to the observation group. papers.title: Distribution of high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) genotypes among women with normal cytology and cervical cancer: a hospital-based cross-sectional study in Mysore, India
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major public health burden in India, with persistent infection by high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) recognized as the primary etiological factor. Understanding the distribution of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) genotypes is essential for optimizing screening and vaccination strategies. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the prevalence and genotype distribution of HR-HPV among women aged 20–75 years attending tertiary care hospitals in Mysore, Karnataka, India. In this hospital-based cross-sectional study, cervicovaginal lavage (CVL) samples were collected from 172 non-pregnant women aged 20–75 years attending the Obstetrics and Gynecology Departments of JSS Hospital and Cheluvamba Hospital, or the Oncology Department of Krishnarajendra Hospital, Mysore, between August 2021 and March 2023. Cheluvamba hospital and Krishnarajendra hospital belongs to Mysore Medical College and Research Institute (MMCRI), Govt of Karnataka, Karnataka, India. Cytological evaluation was performed using the Papanicolaou (Pap) test. HPV DNA was detected by MY09/MY11 polymerase chain reaction (PCR), and HPV-positive participants were genotyped using the TRUPCR ® HR-HPV Genotyping Kit, which detects 14 high-risk HPV genotypes. Of the 172 participants, 117 (68.0%) had normal cytology, while 55 (32.0%) presented with cytological abnormalities or histologically confirmed cervical cancer. Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) was the most common abnormality, accounting for 70.9% of abnormal cases. HPV DNA was detected in 47.0% of women with normal cytology and 80.0% of women with abnormal cytology ( p < 0.05). Genotyping analysis revealed HPV16 as the predominant high-risk genotype in both women with normal cytology and those with cervical cancer. Multiple HPV genotype infections were common, occurring in 49.1% of HPV-positive participants with normal cytology and 59.5% of cervical cancer cases. In addition to HPV16, HPV18, HPV31, HPV58, and HPV59 were among the most frequently detected high-risk genotypes. This hospital-based cross-sectional study provides insights into the distribution of high-risk HPV genotypes among women with normal cytology and cervical cancer in Mysore, India. HPV16 was the predominant genotype in both groups, with multiple HPV infections observed in majority of study participants. These findings contribute to the understanding of regional HPV genotype distribution and recommend the optimization of HPV-based screening strategies and vaccination programs for better outcomes.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 宫颈癌在印度仍是一项主要的公共卫生负担,持续感染高危型人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)被公认为其主要病因。了解高危型HPV基因型的分布对于优化筛查与抗病毒药物治疗策略至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本院基于社区的横断面研究收集了印度卡纳塔克邦迈索尔三级医院就诊的20–75岁172名非孕女性的宫颈阴道灌洗(CVL)样本。在172名参与者中,117人(68.0%)细胞学检查正常,而55人(32.0%)出现细胞学异常或组织学确诊的宫颈癌。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究揭示了印度迈索尔地区细胞学正常女性及宫颈癌前病变人群中高危型HPV基因型的分布特征,可为靶向HPV筛查与抗病毒药物治疗方案的制定提供依据。

papers.title_zh: 印度迈索尔一家医院开展的高危型人乳头瘤病毒(HR-HPV)基因型分布研究:涉及细胞学正常女性及宫颈癌前病变的横断面调查
papers.source_body_en: Cervical cancer remains a major public health burden in India, with persistent infection by high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) recognized as the primary etiological factor. Understanding the distribution of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) genotypes is essential for optimizing screening and vaccination strategies. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the prevalence and genotype distribution of HR-HPV among women aged 20–75 years attending tertiary care hospitals in Mysore, Karnataka, India. In this hospital-based cross-sectional study, cervicovaginal lavage (CVL) samples were collected from 172 non-pregnant women aged 20–75 years attending the Obstetrics and Gynecology Departments of JSS Hospital and Cheluvamba Hospital, or the Oncology Department of Krishnarajendra Hospital, Mysore, between August 2021 and March 2023. Cheluvamba hospital and Krishnarajendra hospital belongs to Mysore Medical College and Research Institute (MMCRI), Govt of Karnataka, Karnataka, India. Cytological evaluation was performed using the Papanicolaou (Pap) test. HPV DNA was detected by MY09/MY11 polymerase chain reaction (PCR), and HPV-positive participants were genotyped using the TRUPCR ® HR-HPV Genotyping Kit, which detects 14 high-risk HPV genotypes. Of the 172 participants, 117 (68.0%) had normal cytology, while 55 (32.0%) presented with cytological abnormalities or histologically confirmed cervical cancer. Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) was the most common abnormality, accounting for 70.9% of abnormal cases. HPV DNA was detected in 47.0% of women with normal cytology and 80.0% of women with abnormal cytology ( p < 0.05). Genotyping analysis revealed HPV16 as the predominant high-risk genotype in both women with normal cytology and those with cervical cancer. Multiple HPV genotype infections were common, occurring in 49.1% of HPV-positive participants with normal cytology and 59.5% of cervical cancer cases. In addition to HPV16, HPV18, HPV31, HPV58, and HPV59 were among the most frequently detected high-risk genotypes. This hospital-based cross-sectional study provides insights into the distribution of high-risk HPV genotypes among women with normal cytology and cervical cancer in Mysore, India. HPV16 was the predominant genotype in both groups, with multiple HPV infections observed in majority of study participants. These findings contribute to the understanding of regional HPV genotype distribution and recommend the optimization of HPV-based screening strategies and vaccination programs for better outcomes.

papers.title: Scaling Adolescent Immunity: Multi-Age Cohort Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Vaccination Campaigns in West Africa—Evidence from Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Liberia, and Sierra Leone
papers.abstract: Background: Cervical cancer remains a major public health problem, causing approximately 660,000 new cases and 348,000 deaths annually, with more than 90% occurring in low- and middle-income countries. The WHO African Region accounts for approximately 20% of global cases and 30% of deaths. In November 2020, the World Health Assembly adopted the Global Strategy for Cervical Cancer Elimination with 90–70–90 targets for 2030. Multi-age cohort (MAC) campaigns have emerged as a high-impact strategy for achieving population-level HPV vaccination coverage. This study documents the implementation and outcomes of HPV MAC campaigns across Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Liberia, and Sierra Leone in 2025. Methods: This multi-country mixed-methods analysis integrated quantitative administrative campaign data with qualitative programmatic assessments across eight operational readiness domains from the WHO Immunization Readiness Assessment Tool. Data were collected between January and December 2025 from national reports, WHO supervision missions, and partner reports. Coverage analysis used administrative data triangulated with independent monitoring. Equity analysis used school enrolment data and geographic accessibility indices. Results: The campaigns targeted 7,376,096 girls aged 9–18 years and reached approximately 6,306,294, achieving 85.5% overall coverage. Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Liberia and Sierra Leone reported administrative coverage of 88.0%, 84.5%, 60.0% and 100%, respectively. All four countries achieved the minimum operational readiness threshold of 80% across all assessed domains. A total of 35,860 health workers were trained, with post-training competency scores increasing from 58.8% to 89.5%. Cold chain functionality exceeded 98% across all campaigns. A total of 314 cases of Adverse Events Following Immunization (AEFIs) were reported, all classified as mild, giving an approximate rate of 5.0 per 100,000 doses. Coverage gaps between in-school and out-of-school girls ranged from 18 to 35 percentage points. Conclusions: The findings suggest that large-scale adolescent HPV immunization can be successfully implemented in resource-limited settings when supported by political commitment, multisectoral coordination and adequate operational resources. The single-dose schedule transition under Gavi 6.0 offers opportunities to simplify delivery. Priority actions include integrating HPV into routine immunization, scaling equity strategies for out-of-school girls and ensuring sustainable financing.

In November 2020, the World Health Assembly adopted the Global Strategy for Cervical Cancer Elimination with 90–70–90 targets for 2030. Multi-age cohort (MAC) campaigns have emerged as a high-impact strategy for achieving population-level HPV vaccination coverage. This study documents the implementation and outcomes of HPV MAC campaigns across Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Liberia, and Sierra Leone in 2025. Methods: This multi-country mixed-methods analysis integrated quantitative administrative campaign data with qualitative programmatic assessments across eight operational readiness domains from the WHO Immunization Readiness Assessment Tool. Data were collected between January and December 2025 from national reports, WHO supervision missions, and partner reports. Coverage analysis used administrative data triangulated with independent monitoring. Equity analysis used school enrolment data and geographic accessibility indices. Results: The campaigns targeted 7,376,096 girls aged 9–18 years and reached approximately 6,306,294, achieving 85.5% overall coverage. Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Liberia and Sierra Leone reported administrative coverage of 88.0%, 84.5%, 60.0% and 100%, respectively. All four countries achieved the minimum operational readiness threshold of 80% across all assessed domains. A total of 35,860 health workers were trained, with post-training competency scores increasing from 58.8% to 89.5%. Cold chain functionality exceeded 98% across all campaigns. A total of 314 cases of Adverse Events Following Immunization (AEFIs) were reported, all classified as mild, giving an approximate rate of 5.0 per 100,000 doses. Coverage gaps between in-school and out-of-school girls ranged from 18 to 35 percentage points. Conclusions: The findings suggest that large-scale adolescent HPV immunization can be successfully implemented in resource-limited settings when supported by political commitment, multisectoral coordination and adequate operational resources. The single-dose schedule transition under Gavi 6.0 offers opportunities to simplify delivery. Priority actions include integrating HPV into routine immunization, scaling equity strategies for out-of-school girls and ensuring sustainable financing.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 宫颈癌 仍是一项重大公共卫生问题,每年导致约 660,000 例新发病例和 348,000 例死亡,其中 90% 以上发生在中低收入国家。本研究记录了 2025 年在科特迪瓦、加纳、利比里亚和塞拉利昂开展的 HPV 多年龄层 队列研究 疫苗接种运动的实施情况及结果。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 多年龄段 队列研究 (MAC) 活动已成为实现人群水平 HPV 疫苗接种 覆盖的高影响力策略。该活动针对 7,376,096 名 9-18 岁女孩,覆盖人数约 6,306,294 人,总体覆盖率达到 85.5%。
elements_zh.methods: 数据收集时间为2025年1月至12月,来源包括国家报告、世界卫生组织督导任务及合作伙伴报告。覆盖率分析采用行政数据与独立监测的三角验证。公平性分析使用学校入学数据和地理可及性指数。
elements_zh.main_results: 科特迪瓦、加纳、利比里亚和塞拉利昂报告的行政覆盖率分别为88.0%、84.5%、60.0%和100%。四国在所有评估领域均达到最低80%运行就绪阈值。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,在政治承诺、多部门协调和充足的运营资源的支持下,大规模青少年 HPV 免疫接种可以在资源有限的环境中成功实施。Gavi 6.0 下的单剂量时间表过渡提供了简化给药的机会。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为在资源有限的环境中实施大规模青少年 HPV 免疫的可行性提供了证据,这可以为未来的 疫苗接种 策略和公共卫生干预措施提供信息。优先行动包括将 HPV 纳入常规免疫接种、扩大失学女童的公平战略以​​及确保可持续融资。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告研究设计的具体限制。该研究提供了多个国家的详细覆盖范围和运营准备数据,因此证据强度很高。

papers.title: Parental knowledge, attitude and acceptability of Human Papillomavirus vaccine: implications for the prevention of cervical cancer in India
papers.abstract: Abstract The Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine is a key tool for cervical cancer prevention; however, vaccine uptake in India remains low despite its recent introduction as a free single-dose vaccine through the public health system. Parental acceptance to vaccination is key to ensure vaccine uptake of adolescent girls. Hence, this study was conducted to assess the knowledge, attitude and acceptability of HPV vaccination parents of adolescent girls, during the early phase of HPV vaccine rollout. This community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 422 parents of adolescent girls, during the early phase of HPV vaccine rollout in the country, to assess their knowledge, attitude and acceptability of HPV vaccination. Only 18.2% of participants had heard of HPV infection, 6.6% identified HPV as the primary cause of cervical cancer, and 8.5% had heard of the HPV vaccine, with only 5.9% demonstrated good knowledge of vaccination. Despite limited knowledge, 48.8% had a positive attitude, 62.6% demonstrated good acceptability, and 72.7% expressed willingness for vaccination. Higher parental education and healthcare-related occupations were associated with greater vaccine acceptability in bivariate analysis. Significant positive correlations were observed among knowledge of HPV infection and cervical cancer, HPV vaccine knowledge, attitudes, and vaccine acceptability ( p < 0.001). These findings highlight persistent knowledge gaps despite moderate-to-high acceptability. Targeted interventions using community health workers (ASHAs) and digital platforms are needed to improve informed decision-making and support equitable HPV vaccine uptake in disadvantaged settings, contributing to India’s cervical cancer elimination goals.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the low HPV vaccine uptake in India by examining parental knowledge, attitude, and acceptability of HPV vaccination for adolescent girls. This is critical for preventing cervical cancer, as HPV is a primary cause of the disease.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 422 parents of adolescent girls during the early phase of HPV vaccine rollout in India to assess their knowledge, attitude, and acceptability of HPV vaccination.
analysis.methods: The study used a structured questionnaire to evaluate participants' knowledge of HPV infection, cervical cancer, and the vaccine. Bivariate analysis was employed to examine associations between parental education, occupation, and vaccine acceptability.
analysis.main_results: Only 18.2% of participants had heard of HPV infection, 6.6% identified HPV as the primary cause of cervical cancer, and 8.5% had heard of the HPV vaccine. Despite limited knowledge, 48.8% had a positive attitude, 62.6% demonstrated good acceptability, and 72.7% expressed willingness for vaccination.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate a significant knowledge gap about HPV and its association with cervical cancer, even though there is moderate-to-high acceptability of the vaccine among parents. This highlights the need for targeted interventions to improve informed decision-making.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides insights into the factors influencing parental acceptability of HPV vaccination, which can inform strategies to enhance vaccine uptake and support India’s cervical cancer elimination goals.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which cannot establish causality. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on self-reported data and bivariate analysis without controlling for confounding variables.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates parental knowledge, attitude, and acceptability of the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine in India, focusing on its role in preventing cervical cancer. Conducted as a community-based cross-sectional survey among 422 parents of adolescent girls during the early phase of HPV vaccine rollout, the research reveals significant gaps in understanding HPV and its link to cervical cancer, despite moderate-to-high vaccine acceptability. The study highlights the importance of parental education and healthcare-related occupations in influencing vaccine acceptability. These findings underscore the need for targeted interventions, such as those involving community health workers and digital platforms, to improve informed decision-making and ensure equitable vaccine uptake. The evidence is moderate due to the cross-sectional design and lack of control for confounding factors, which limits the ability to draw definitive causal conclusions.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在印度 HPV 疫苗 推广的早期阶段,对 422 名青春期女孩的父母进行了一项基于社区的横断面研究,以评估他们对 HPV 疫苗接种 的知识、态度和可接受性。
elements_zh.methods: 研究采用结构化问卷评估参与者对HPV感染、宫颈癌及HPV疫苗的认知。通过双变量分析探讨父母受教育程度、职业与HPV疫苗接种可接受度的关联。
elements_zh.main_results: 只有 18.2% 的参与者听说过 HPV 感染,6.6% 的参与者认为 HPV 是 宫颈癌 的主要原因,8.5% 的参与者听说过 HPV 疫苗。尽管了解有限,但48.8%的人持积极态度,62.6%的人表现出良好的接受度,72.7%的人表示愿意使用疫苗接种。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,尽管家长对 疫苗 的接受度为中等到高,但有关 HPV 及其与 宫颈癌 的关联的知识仍存在显着差距。这凸显了采取有针对性的干预措施以改善知情决策的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究深入了解了影响父母对 HPV 疫苗接种 可接受性的因素,这可以为提高 疫苗 吸收率和支持印度 宫颈癌 消除目标的策略提供参考。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到横截面设计的限制,无法确定因果关系。证据是中等的,因为它基于自我报告的数据和双变量分析,没有控制混杂变量。

papers.title_zh: 父母对人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)疫苗的认知、态度及可接受度:对印度宫颈癌预防的启示
papers.source_body_en: Abstract The Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine is a key tool for cervical cancer prevention; however, vaccine uptake in India remains low despite its recent introduction as a free single-dose vaccine through the public health system. Parental acceptance to vaccination is key to ensure vaccine uptake of adolescent girls. Hence, this study was conducted to assess the knowledge, attitude and acceptability of HPV vaccination parents of adolescent girls, during the early phase of HPV vaccine rollout. This community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 422 parents of adolescent girls, during the early phase of HPV vaccine rollout in the country, to assess their knowledge, attitude and acceptability of HPV vaccination. Only 18.2% of participants had heard of HPV infection, 6.6% identified HPV as the primary cause of cervical cancer, and 8.5% had heard of the HPV vaccine, with only 5.9% demonstrated good knowledge of vaccination. Despite limited knowledge, 48.8% had a positive attitude, 62.6% demonstrated good acceptability, and 72.7% expressed willingness for vaccination. Higher parental education and healthcare-related occupations were associated with greater vaccine acceptability in bivariate analysis. Significant positive correlations were observed among knowledge of HPV infection and cervical cancer, HPV vaccine knowledge, attitudes, and vaccine acceptability ( p < 0.001). These findings highlight persistent knowledge gaps despite moderate-to-high acceptability. Targeted interventions using community health workers (ASHAs) and digital platforms are needed to improve informed decision-making and support equitable HPV vaccine uptake in disadvantaged settings, contributing to India’s cervical cancer elimination goals.

papers.title: Prevalence of human papillomavirus in the public health system of the central-northern region of Chile
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE Previously, we found a high prevalence of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) in women attending the private health system. Therefore, the objective of this study was to determine the frequency of HR-HPV in a large cohort of women attending the public health system and to compare these findings. METHODS A total of 39,512 cervical samples from women aged 18 to 91 years who attended gynecological check-ups between 2020 and 2024 were analyzed using qPCR and the Papanicolaou technique. RESULTS The overall prevalence of HR-HPV infection between 2020 and 2024 was 13.70% (95% CI: 13.37-14.05%), with annual values of 13.07%, 12.64%, 14.80%, 14.24%, and 14.15% in 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024, respectively. In women under 25 years of age, the prevalence of HR-HPV was 34.03% during the evaluated period, compared to 16.35% in women aged 25 to 44 years, 10.47% in those aged 45 to 64 years, and 11.52% in women over 64 years of age. Pap smears showed 89.71% NILM results in HPV-negative women, compared to 74.59% in HPV-positive women. The rates of LSIL and HSIL were 0.14% and 0.07% in HPV-negative women, respectively; however, these values increased to 4.73% and 4.43% in HPV-positive women, respectively. Probable carcinoma was found in only 0.006% of HPV-negative women, but in 0.46% of HPV-positive women. CONCLUSIONS The prevalence of HR-HPV infection in women attending the public health system in the central-northern region appears to be similar to that previously reported in Chile, but lower than that reported in the same region for women attending the private health system.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed to determine the frequency of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) in women attending the public health system, as previous research had found a high prevalence in the private health system.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study analyzed 39,512 cervical samples from women aged 18 to 91 years who attended gynecological check-ups between 2020 and 2024 in the central-northern region of Chile.
analysis.methods: Samples were analyzed using qPCR and the Papanicolaou technique to detect HR-HPV infection and cytological abnormalities.
analysis.main_results: The overall prevalence of HR-HPV infection was 13.70% (95% CI: 13.37-14.05%), with higher rates in women under 25 years (34.03%) compared to older age groups. HPV-positive women had significantly higher rates of LSIL (4.73% vs. 0.14%) and HSIL (4.43% vs. 0.07%) than HPV-negative women.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that HR-HPV prevalence in the public health system was similar to previously reported national rates but lower than in the private health system in the same region, highlighting potential disparities in HPV infection rates between healthcare systems.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Findings inform public health surveillance and resource allocation by providing age-stratified prevalence data, which can guide targeted screening and prevention strategies for HPV-related diseases in the public health system.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's strength lies in its large sample size and longitudinal design, but limitations include potential selection bias as only women attending gynecological check-ups were included, and the evidence is moderate due to the abstract-only nature of the report.

analysis.summary_en: This study determined the prevalence of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) in 39,512 women attending Chile's public health system between 2020-2024. The overall HR-HPV prevalence was 13.70%, with significantly higher rates in women under 25 years (34.03%) compared to older age groups. HPV-positive women had markedly increased rates of cytological abnormalities, including LSIL (4.73% vs. 0.14%) and HSIL (4.43% vs. 0.07%) compared to HPV-negative women. The prevalence was similar to national rates but lower than previously reported in the private health system, suggesting potential healthcare disparities. These findings provide valuable data for public health planning and targeted screening programs.

papers.title_zh: 智利中北部地区公共卫生系统中的患病率 人乳头瘤病毒
papers.source_body_en: OBJECTIVE Previously, we found a high prevalence of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) in women attending the private health system. Therefore, the objective of this study was to determine the frequency of HR-HPV in a large cohort of women attending the public health system and to compare these findings. METHODS A total of 39,512 cervical samples from women aged 18 to 91 years who attended gynecological check-ups between 2020 and 2024 were analyzed using qPCR and the Papanicolaou technique. RESULTS The overall prevalence of HR-HPV infection between 2020 and 2024 was 13.70% (95% CI: 13.37-14.05%), with annual values of 13.07%, 12.64%, 14.80%, 14.24%, and 14.15% in 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024, respectively. In women under 25 years of age, the prevalence of HR-HPV was 34.03% during the evaluated period, compared to 16.35% in women aged 25 to 44 years, 10.47% in those aged 45 to 64 years, and 11.52% in women over 64 years of age. Pap smears showed 89.71% NILM results in HPV-negative women, compared to 74.59% in HPV-positive women. The rates of LSIL and HSIL were 0.14% and 0.07% in HPV-negative women, respectively; however, these values increased to 4.73% and 4.43% in HPV-positive women, respectively. Probable carcinoma was found in only 0.006% of HPV-negative women, but in 0.46% of HPV-positive women. CONCLUSIONS The prevalence of HR-HPV infection in women attending the public health system in the central-northern region appears to be similar to that previously reported in Chile, but lower than that reported in the same region for women attending the private health system.

papers.title: 03 | Knowledge about human papillomavirus and its vaccination and willingness to accept human papillomavirus vaccination in a population of students from the Local Health Authorities of Agrigento, Palermo and Trapani, Western Sicily
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is one of the most common sexually transmitted infection and is associated with the development of several diseases, including malignancies such as cervical, anal, vulvar, vaginal penile, oropharyngeal cancers and benign lesions such as genital warts. HPV vaccination is a highly effective and safe primary prevention intervention; however, uptake of vaccination programs is strongly influenced by the level of knowledge and perceptions of the target population, particularly among adolescents. In this context, educational interventions at schools play a central role in promoting awareness and favorable attitudes toward preventive behaviors. Materials and Methods. The study involved a sample of 2,146 students attending first and second grade secondary schools in the 3 Wester Sicily provinces of Agrigento, Palermo and Trapani. Participants were involved via the administration of a structured questionnaire designed to assess their knowledge, attitudes toward HPV and its vaccination, and willingness to receive vaccination. A second version of the questionnaire was re-administered following training sessions aimed to providing scientific information on the infection and prevention strategies. Responses were collected using Likert scales ranging from 1 to 5 to assess opinions and from 1 to 10 to measure vaccination willingness. Participation in the study required a written informed consent previously signed from the students' parents. Students showed a high level of agreement with the statement that the virus can cause serious illness, with an average score of 4.5 out of 5, and acknowledged the possibility of being exposed to the infection during their lifetime, with an average score of 3.9. A strong perception of the importance of communication on the topic also emerged, both within the family, school, and healthcare settings, with average scores of 4.23, 4.46, and 4.21, respectively. Regarding the Vaccination, participants expressed a high level of agreement regarding the vaccine's usefulness in preventing cervical cancer and genital warts (mean 4.5), its safety (mean 4.32), and the appropriateness of their peers getting vaccinated (mean 4.48). analysis.research_question_and_background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a common sexually transmitted infection linked to various diseases, including cancers and benign lesions, highlighting the need for understanding its impact and vaccination willingness in a specific population.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in three Western Sicily provinces (Agrigento, Palermo, and Trapani) involving 2,146 students from first and second grade secondary schools.
analysis.methods: Participants completed a structured questionnaire to assess their knowledge, attitudes, and willingness to accept HPV vaccination, with a second version administered after training sessions to provide scientific information.
analysis.main_results: Students showed high agreement with the statement that HPV can cause serious illness (mean score 4.5) and acknowledged lifetime exposure risk (mean score 3.9). Vaccination willingness increased from 8.62 to 8.94 on a 1-10 scale (p-value < 0.05).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate that educational interventions can enhance students' understanding and willingness to accept HPV vaccination, particularly regarding its role in preventing cervical cancer and genital warts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that targeted educational efforts in schools could improve HPV vaccination uptake, contributing to public health strategies aimed at reducing HPV-related diseases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a single population and relies on self-reported data, which may introduce bias. However, the evidence is strong due to the use of structured questionnaires and statistical analysis of the results.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the knowledge, attitudes, and willingness to accept human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination among 2,146 students in Western Sicily. It found that students had a high level of agreement regarding HPV's association with serious illnesses and its prevention through vaccination. Educational interventions significantly increased vaccination willingness, with a mean score rising from 8.62 to 8.94 on a 1-10 scale. The study highlights the importance of school-based education in promoting HPV vaccination, particularly for preventing cervical cancer and genital warts. However, the study's reliance on self-reported data and its focus on a single population may limit the generalizability of the findings. The evidence is strong, as it includes structured questionnaires and statistical analysis, but further research is needed to confirm these results in broader contexts.

In this context, educational interventions at schools play a central role in promoting awareness and favorable attitudes toward preventive behaviors. Materials and Methods. papers.title: High-risk HPV detection via GeneXpert in self-collected anal swabs among MSM living with HIV: Insights from a cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Men who have sex with men living with HIV (MSMLWHIV) have a high risk of persistent high-risk HPV infection, and rapid tools like Xpert HPV can help expand screening in low-resource settings. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess the feasibility of using self-collected anal swabs for detecting high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infections in MSMLWHIV, using the Xpert® HPV assay. Additionally, we investigated factors associated with HR-HPV positivity. DESIGN: This was a single-center cross-sectional study conducted from 22nd May 2024 to 31st July 2024 among MSMLWHIV in Bamako. METHODS: Participants were recruited from the Soutoura NGO in Bamako, Mali. To be eligible, individuals had to be HIV-1 positive, on antiretroviral therapy, 18 years or older, and self-identified as MSM. The prevalence of HR-HPV was reported by sociodemographic characteristics and sexual behaviors. We used a penalized logistic regression model using Firth's method to identify sociodemographic and behavioral factors associated with HR-HPV positivity. RESULTS: A total of 245 MSMLWHIV were initially tested. Of these, 170 yielded successful results and were subsequently included in the study analysis. The participants had a median age of 26 years (IQR 24-29) with the median age of first anal intercourse at 16 years (IQR 16-18). Among the participants, 29% (49/170) identified as bisexual, 42% (72/170) reported never using condoms, 16% (27/170) participated in group intercourse, and 42% (71/170) had at least two different sexual partners in the past six months. Among those successfully tested, 65% (110/170) were positive for HR-HPV, with HPV16 detected in 12% (21/170) of participants. No or primary education and consistent condom use were associated with lower odds of HR-HPV positivity, while the unexpected association observed with smoking should be interpreted with caution. CONCLUSION: The high HR-HPV prevalence among MSMLWHIV calls for targeted screening and prevention. Although Xpert HPV shows promise, the 31% failure rate with self-collected samples underscores the need for improvements in sample collection procedures and technical performance.

papers.title_zh: 在感染HIV的男男性行为者中通过GeneXpert检测自采肛拭子中的高危型HPV:一项横断面研究的见解
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Men who have sex with men living with HIV (MSMLWHIV) have a high risk of persistent high-risk HPV infection, and rapid tools like Xpert HPV can help expand screening in low-resource settings. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess the feasibility of using self-collected anal swabs for detecting high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infections in MSMLWHIV, using the Xpert® HPV assay. Additionally, we investigated factors associated with HR-HPV positivity. DESIGN: This was a single-center cross-sectional study conducted from 22nd May 2024 to 31st July 2024 among MSMLWHIV in Bamako. METHODS: Participants were recruited from the Soutoura NGO in Bamako, Mali. To be eligible, individuals had to be HIV-1 positive, on antiretroviral therapy, 18 years or older, and self-identified as MSM. The prevalence of HR-HPV was reported by sociodemographic characteristics and sexual behaviors. We used a penalized logistic regression model using Firth's method to identify sociodemographic and behavioral factors associated with HR-HPV positivity. RESULTS: A total of 245 MSMLWHIV were initially tested. Of these, 170 yielded successful results and were subsequently included in the study analysis. The participants had a median age of 26 years (IQR 24-29) with the median age of first anal intercourse at 16 years (IQR 16-18). Among the participants, 29% (49/170) identified as bisexual, 42% (72/170) reported never using condoms, 16% (27/170) participated in group intercourse, and 42% (71/170) had at least two different sexual partners in the past six months. Among those successfully tested, 65% (110/170) were positive for HR-HPV, with HPV16 detected in 12% (21/170) of participants. No or primary education and consistent condom use were associated with lower odds of HR-HPV positivity, while the unexpected association observed with smoking should be interpreted with caution. CONCLUSION: The high HR-HPV prevalence among MSMLWHIV calls for targeted screening and prevention. Although Xpert HPV shows promise, the 31% failure rate with self-collected samples underscores the need for improvements in sample collection procedures and technical performance.

papers.title: Atomic resolution structure of human papillomavirus bound to heparin
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a significant health burden and leading cause of virus-induced cancers. The mechanisms of HPV receptor binding and host entry are not completely understood, although it is known that heparan sulfate proteoglycans (HSPGs) mediate entry. HPV16 quasivirus, composed of L1 and L2 capsid proteins with a packaged cottontail rabbit papillomavirus genome was incubated with heparin. The complex was vitrified, and data were collected for cryoEM single particle analysis. Subparticles were extracted and hexavalent and pentavalent capsomers were refined separately. Here we present the resulting 1.9 Å resolution structure, with heparin visualized around the capsomer at the icosahedral fivefold vertex. A model of the asymmetric unit was built unambiguously into the atomic resolution cryoEM map. Hydrogen bonds are predicted between L1 N-terminal regions, which are supported by molecular dynamics. The heparin binding site was identified, along with local L1 conformational changes and global flexibility changes. These changes induced by heparin binding likely reflect the structure of HPV during early stages of entry and provide a framework for future HPV biochemical, genetic, and biophysical studies. Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a significant health burden, but the mechanisms of HPV receptor binding are not understood. Here, the authors solve a 1.9 Å resolution structure of HPV bound to heparin with insights into the binding interface.

papers.title: A Cell-Penetrating Peptide and Signal Sequence Fusion DNA Vaccine Enhances CD8+ T Cell-Mediated Anti-Tumor Immunity Targeting HPV-16 Cervical Cancer Antigens.
papers.abstract: Background Cervical cancer is the fourth most common cancer affecting women, with almost all cases caused by infection with Human Papillomavirus (HPV). Previous research has explored the potential of cell-penetrating peptides to improve the efficacy of peptide vaccines and signal peptide sequences to increase protein secretion in DNA vaccines. In this study, we evaluated the in vivo efficacy of DNA vaccines targeting HPV-16 E6 and E7 viral antigens that are constructed with both a cell-penetrating peptide and IL-2 signal peptide to improve immunogenicity. Results We generated DNA vaccine constructs utilizing combinations of E7(49-57), E6(48-57), IL-2 signal sequence (sig), 9-polyarginine (9R), and 12-polyarginine (12R) cloned into pcDNA3 vectors. Transfection of the pcDNA3-sig9RE7, pcDNA3-sig12RE7, or pcDNA3-9RE7 vaccine constructs induced a significant E7-specific CD8+ T cell response in vitro. We observed that the pcDNA3-sig9RE7 vaccine induced the strongest E7-specific immune response in vivo compared to the pcDNA3-9RE7 and pcDNA3-sig12RE7 constructs. We demonstrated the potential protective and therapeutic anti-tumor effects of the pcDNA3-sig9RE7 vaccination against the HPV-16 E7 expressing TC-1 tumor model in mice. Finally, we found similar anti-tumor effects for the pcDNA3-sig9RE6 vaccine which suggest this DNA vaccine strategy could be applied to various cervical cancer antigens. Conclusion Treatment with the pcDNA3-sig9RE7 DNA vaccine induces a potent E7-specific anti-tumor immune response in mice. By demonstrating the potential of utilizing a cell-penetrating peptide and signal peptide sequence in combination to improve efficacy, this study provides a foundation for future research into fusion DNA vaccines with cell-penetrating peptides and signal peptide combinations.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 宫颈癌 是影响女性的第四大常见癌症,几乎所有病例都是由 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染引起。先前的研究探索了细胞穿透肽提高肽 疫苗 功效的潜力,以及信号肽序列增加 DNA 疫苗 中蛋白质分泌的潜力。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在这项研究中,我们评估了 DNA 疫苗 靶向 HPV-16 E6 和 E7 病毒抗原的体内功效,这些抗原由细胞穿透肽和 IL-2 信号肽构建,以提高免疫原性。
elements_zh.methods: 我们利用克隆到 pcDNA3 媒介 中的 E7(49-57)、E6(48-57)、IL-2 信号序列 (sig)、9-聚精氨酸 (9R) 和 12-聚精氨酸 (12R) 的组合生成 DNA 疫苗 构建体。
elements_zh.main_results: pcDNA3-sig9RE7、pcDNA3-sig12RE7 或 pcDNA3-9RE7 疫苗 构建体的转染在体外诱导显着的 E7 特异性 CD8+ T 细胞反应。我们观察到,与 pcDNA3-9RE7 和 pcDNA3-sig12RE7 构建体相比,pcDNA3-sig9RE7 疫苗 在体内诱导最强的 E7 特异性 免疫应答。我们证明了 pcDNA3-sig9RE7 疫苗接种 对小鼠中表达 HPV-16 E7 的 TC-1 肿瘤模型的潜在保护和治疗性抗肿瘤作用。最后,我们发现 pcDNA3-sig9RE6 疫苗 具有类似的抗肿瘤作用,这表明该 DNA 疫苗 策略可以应用于各种 宫颈癌 抗原。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 治疗与pcDNA3-sig9RE7 DNA 疫苗在小鼠体内可诱导强效E7特异性抗肿瘤免疫应答。通过展示细胞穿透肽与信号肽序列联合应用以提升疗效的潜力,本研究为未来融合DNA 疫苗与细胞穿透肽及信号肽组合的研究奠定了基础。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究为融合DNA 疫苗与细胞穿透肽及信号肽组合的未来研究奠定了基础,该策略有望增强针对HPV相关宫颈癌的免疫原性及抗肿瘤免疫。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据未报告本研究的局限性。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景 宫颈癌是女性第四常见癌症,几乎所有病例均由感染人乳头瘤病毒(人乳头瘤病毒,HPV)引起。早期研究已探索细胞穿透肽在提升肽疫苗疗效及信号肽在增强DNA 疫苗蛋白分泌中的潜力。本研究评估了靶向HPV-16 E6和E7病毒抗原的DNA 疫苗在体内疗效,该DNA构建了细胞穿透肽与IL-2信号肽融合以提高免疫原性。结果 我们构建了多种DNA 疫苗载体,包括E7(49-57)、E6(48-57)、IL-2信号序列(sig)、9-聚精氨酸(9R)及12-聚精氨酸(12R),并将其克隆至pcDNA3 媒介载体。转染pcDNA3-sig9RE7、pcDNA3-sig12RE7或pcDNA3-9RE7 疫苗载体后,体外可诱导显著的E7特异性CD8+ T细胞应答。研究发现,与pcDNA3-9RE7及pcDNA3-sig12RE7载体相比,pcDNA3-sig9RE7 疫苗在体内诱导了最强的E7特异性免疫应答。我们证明了pcDNA3-sig9RE7 疫苗在小鼠HPV-16 E7表达TC-1肿瘤模型中具有潜在的保护性及治疗性抗肿瘤效应。最后,我们发现pcDNA3-sig9RE6 疫苗同样具有类似的抗肿瘤效应,提示该DNA 疫苗策略可应用于多种宫颈癌抗原。结论 治疗与pcDNA3-sig9RE7 DNA 疫苗在小鼠体内可诱导强效E7特异性抗肿瘤免疫应答。通过展示细胞穿透肽与信号肽序列联合应用以提升疗效的潜力,本研究为未来融合DNA 疫苗与细胞穿透肽及信号肽组合的研究奠定了基础。

papers.title: Coreactant-specific electrochemiluminescence of an anthracene-based zinc framework for detection of HPV-16 DNA.
papers.abstract: The efficient activation of a coreactant is challenging in electrochemiluminescence (ECL) enhancement. Herein, a metal-organic framework nanoemitter was designed with an anthracene derivative as a luminophore ligand and a Zn 2+ node. It demonstrated a 1,4-diazabicyclo[2.2.2]octane (DABCO)-specific ECL pathway via coordination interaction between the coreactant and the Zn 2+ node, which significantly enhanced emission over conventional coreactants, establishing a sensitive strategy for DNA detection.

papers.title: Long-term risk of cancer following cervical intraepithelial neoplasia: A significant study leveraging Taiwan's national health insurance research database
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: We used Taiwan's national health insurance research database to conduct a study on the risk of cancer after cervical intraepithelial neoplasia. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The study analyzed data from the Taiwan NHIRD comparing three cohorts: one with precancerous cervical dysplasia (CIN2+ dysplasia), one with mild dysplasia or undetermined dysplasia (non-CIN2+ dysplasia), and one without dysplasia. analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the long-term risk of cancer following cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, addressing the need to understand the association between precancerous lesions and subsequent malignancies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used Taiwan's national health insurance research database to compare three cohorts: those with precancerous cervical dysplasia (CIN2+ dysplasia), those with mild dysplasia or undetermined dysplasia (non-CIN2+ dysplasia), and those without dysplasia. The analysis included 776, 1248, and 14,421 new cases in these cohorts, respectively.
analysis.methods: The study excluded patients with index dates before 2001 or after 2016 and adjusted for various factors to analyze future cancer risks. It used competing hazard ratios to assess the risk of different cancer types across the cohorts.
analysis.main_results: The competing hazard ratios (95% CI) for cancer risk were 2.312 (2.112-2.53) for the CIN2+ cohort and 1.195 (1.104-1.293) for the non-CIN2+ cohort, with significant differences observed for several cancer types.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that moderate or severe cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and carcinoma in situ significantly increase long-term cancer risk, even after surgical intervention, highlighting the importance of ongoing monitoring.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings emphasize the need for consistent surveillance and management of patients with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia to mitigate long-term cancer risks, particularly for high-risk HPV-related malignancies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on a national health insurance database, which may have biases or missing data, and the evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study leveraged Taiwan's national health insurance research database to examine the long-term cancer risk following cervical intraepithelial neoplasia. It compared three cohorts: those with moderate or severe dysplasia (CIN2+), those with mild or undetermined dysplasia (non-CIN2+), and those without dysplasia. The results showed significantly elevated cancer risks in the CIN2+ cohort compared to the non-CIN2+ and control groups, with hazard ratios indicating a higher likelihood of various cancers, including cervical, anogenital, and head and neck cancers. The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that even after surgical intervention, CIN2+ and carcinoma in situ are associated with increased cancer risk, underscoring the importance of continued monitoring. The study's evidence is moderate due to its observational design and potential database limitations, but it provides valuable insights into the long-term implications of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia for cancer surveillance and management.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus (HPV) in primary lung cancer patients in Eastern India, addressing the knowledge gap regarding HPV's role in lung cancer.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study was conducted in Eastern India between 2022 and 2024, involving 150 patients diagnosed with primary lung cancer.
analysis.methods: HPV DNA was detected using polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and genotyping was performed through sequencing to identify specific HPV types present in the lung cancer specimens.
analysis.main_results: HPV was detected in 12% of the lung cancer specimens, with HPV16 being the most prevalent genotype, accounting for 75% of the positive cases.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest a potential association between HPV16 and lung cancer in this population, highlighting the need for further research to explore this link.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study contributes to understanding the role of HPV in lung cancer, which could inform targeted screening and prevention strategies in high-risk populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and the sample size may not be sufficient to generalize findings to broader populations. The evidence is moderate in strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus (HPV) in primary lung cancer patients in Eastern India. It found that 12% of lung cancer specimens tested positive for HPV, with HPV16 being the most common genotype. The research highlights the potential role of HPV16 in lung cancer, suggesting a need for further studies to explore this association. The study's cross-sectional design and relatively small sample size limit the strength of the evidence, which is considered moderate. These findings may inform future screening and prevention strategies for HPV-related cancers in this region.
