media_mentions.content_title: Prevalence and Genotype Distribution of Human Papillomavirus in Primary Lung Cancer in Eastern India
media_mentions.content: Abstract Background: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-associated mortality globally, with approximately 2.5 million new cases and 1.8 million deaths. It accounts for approximately one in five cancer-related deaths worldwide. While tobacco smoking is the main cause of lung cancer, many cases occur in never-smokers, indicating that other environmental, genetic, and infectious contributors may play a role. High-risk human papillomavirus (HPV), particularly HPV-16 and -18, is a known etiologic agent in cervical, anogenital, and oropharyngeal malignancies. The pathogenic role of HPV in lung cancer remains controversial, mainly due to significant geographical variation in prevalence and inconsistent detection rates, despite increasing molecular evidence of HPV DNA in primary lung tumors. Information about HPV-related lung cancer in India is scarce. Objectives: This study aims to determine the prevalence of high-risk HPV types 16 and 18 in primary lung cancer tissue samples and to evaluate their potential associations with clinicodemographic characteristics. Materials and methods: A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted using samples collected between January 2023 and October 2025 at a tertiary care teaching hospital in eastern India. A total of 95 archival formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue specimens from histopathologically confirmed primary lung neoplasms were included in the study. DNA was extracted from FFPE tissues and subjected to real-time polymerase chain reaction for HPV-16 and HPV-18. We compared clinicodemographic variables between HPV-positive and HPV-negative patients. Results: HPV-16 DNA was detected in 29 of 95 (30.5%) lung cancer specimens, whereas HPV-18 was not detected in any case. Squamous cell carcinoma showed a higher HPV-16 positivity rate than adenocarcinoma (42.1% vs. 26.8%), although the difference was not statistically significant. HPV-positive patients had a mean age of 64 years and were predominantly male. Smoking was significantly associated with HPV positivity (p = 0.035). Most HPV-positive tumors involved the right lung and occurred among rural residents. Conclusions: Of primary lung cancers in this cohort, one third were HPV-16 positive, and none were HPV-18 positive. These findings suggest a possible association between HPV-16 infection and pulmonary carcinoma, particularly among smokers. Future larger multicenter studies may clarify the biological relevance of HPV in lung carcinogenesis by incorporating detailed viral oncogene expression and genotyping. Introduction Lung cancer is the second most commonly diagnosed malignancy. It continues to be the leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide, accounting for nearly one in every five cancer deaths [1,2]. The five-year survival remains dismal because most patients present with advanced disease [2], despite remarkable advances in imaging, molecular diagnostics, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy. Although tobacco smoking is still the main etiological factor, about 10-25% of lung cancers develop in individuals with little or no history of smoking, suggesting that other environmental, occupational, genetic, and/or infectious factors may enhance pulmonary carcinogenesis [3,4]. Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a small, double-stranded, non-enveloped DNA virus from the Papillomaviridae family. Over 220 different HPV genotypes have been characterized to date, with HPV-16 and HPV-18 contributing to almost 70% of cervical cancers, as well as a range of noncervical malignancies, such as anogenital (vulva, vagina, penis, and anus) and oropharyngeal cancers [5]. Infection with these high-risk HPV types of HPV leads to malignant transformation due to expression of the viral oncoproteins E6 and E7, which bind to and inactivate the tumor suppressor proteins p53 and retinoblastoma, causing loss of contact inhibition, self-sufficient cell replication, insensitivity to growth inhibitory signals, evasion of apoptosis, chromosomal instability, and accumulation of mutations during cellular proliferation [5,6]. The role of HPV in lung carcinogenesis has been debated. This association was first proposed by Syrjänen in 1979 after demonstrating HPV-associated cytopathic changes within the bronchial epithelium [7]. Following this observation, HPV DNA has been studied in primary lung tumors, and the prevalence has been found to range from 0% to more than 60%, reflecting high variability in study design, geographical distribution, molecular detection methods, and sample selection [8,9]. A recent systematic review and meta-analysis estimated an overall HPV prevalence of ~13.5% in more than 9,000 lung cancer patients, with higher rates detected in Asia compared to Europe or North America [10]. In most of these studies, HPV-16 has been consistently observed as the predominant type, with less frequent detection of HPV-18 [10,11]. The varied geographical distribution of HPV genotypes highlights the need for more studies to clarify the prevalence and clinical impact of HPV in lung cancer in various populations. In India, most of the pivotal research conducted on HPV-related cancers has focused only on cervical cancer, and data regarding the HPV infection status in lung cancer is still very sparse. This study was conducted to assess the prevalence of high-risk HPV genotypes (HPV-16 and HPV-18) in patients with histopathologically proven primary lung cancer using real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) at a tertiary care center in eastern India and to examine the association between HPV positivity and various clinicodemographic variables. Materials & Methods This retrospective cross-sectional observational study was conducted on samples between January 2023 and October 2025 in the Departments of Microbiology, Pulmonary Medicine, and Pathology at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Bhubaneswar, India, which started on January 21, 2025, in accordance with the principles of the Declaration of Helsinki [12]. The HPV DNA testing was not done at the time of diagnosis of lung cancer; rather, all the samples collected over three years were tested later. Ethical approval was obtained from the Institutional Ethics Committee of AIIMS, Bhubaneswar (approval number: IEC/AIIMS BBSR/PG Thesis/2023-24/153). Study population Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue samples obtained from patients who were diagnosed with primary lung carcinoma by histopathology were included. An experienced pulmonary pathologist selected representative tumor-rich regions within each FFPE tissue block. Exclusion criteria were metastatic lung malignancies, pulmonary sarcomas, recurrent tumors, or tissue blocks with insufficient material for DNA extraction. Sample size calculation The required sample size was calculated taking an approximate frequency of 25% using the following equation: n=z2αpqd2 where p is the expected proportion of HPV-16 and HPV-18 in the cases (6.3), q is the expected proportion of other types of HPV (93.7), and d is the desired level of precision (5), which gave a sample size (n) of 94. The minimum required sample size was calculated to be 94; consequently, a total of 95 eligible cases were enrolled. DNA extraction and HPV detection Genomic DNA was extracted using the QIAamp DNA FFPE Tissue Kit (QIAGEN, Hilden, Germany) according to the manufacturer's instructions. DNA quantity and quality were assessed using a NanoDrop spectrophotometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc., Waltham, MA, USA) by measuring absorbance at 260 and 280 nm. Detection of high-risk HPV genotypes 16 and 18 by real-time PCR using commercially available primers and probes (TRUPCR HPV-16 and HPV-18 detection kit, 3B BlackBio Dx Ltd, India) was performed according to the manufacturer's instructions along with appropriate positive and no-template controls as provided in the kit. The study workflow is shown in Figure 1. Data collection and statistical analysis Clinical and demographic data were obtained from hospital medical records, including age, sex, smoking history, passive smoking, area of residence, histological subtype, side of the involved lung, and survival status. Histological diagnosis and subtype evaluation of lung cancer were performed in accordance with the current World Health Organization classification of thoracic tumors. Data were organized in Excel (Microsoft Corp., Redmond, WA, USA) and analyzed using SPSS Statistics version 26.0 (IBM Corp., Released 2019; IBM SPSS Statistics for Windows, Version 26.0; Armonk, NY, USA). Depending on whether the data were normally distributed, the quantitative results were reported as the mean and standard deviation or as the median with the interquartile range. The proportion and confidence interval were used to display the categorical data. The independent-samples Student's t-test was used for normally distributed continuous variables, while the categorical variables were compared using the Chi-square test or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate. Bivariate logistic regression was used to identify the risk factors associated with the development of high-risk HPV. In the multivariable analysis, the p-value threshold was set at <0.05 to indicate statistical significance. Results A total of 95 patients with histopathologically confirmed primary lung carcinoma were included (Table 1). The mean age of the study population was 61.4 ± 11.4 years (age range 28-83 years). Most patients were male (69; 72.6%), yielding an overall male-to-female ratio of approximately 2.7:1. Rural residents accounted for 78.9% of the study population. Smoking history was present in 52.6% of patients, while passive smoking was reported by 13.7%. The right lung was more frequently involved (62.1%) than the left lung (31.5%). Bilateral disease occurred in only two patients (2.1%). At the end of the follow-up period, mortality was observed in 30.5% of patients. Histopathological distribution Non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) accounted for the majority of tumors (90/95). Adenocarcinoma was the predominant subtype (71, 74.7%), followed by squamous cell carcinoma (19, 20.0%). Three cases were classified as NSCLC-not otherwise specified (NOS), while two patients had small cell lung carcinoma (SCLC). Among the 95 lung cancer specimens, 29 (30.5%) tested positive for HPV-16 DNA. None of the samples demonstrated HPV-18 DNA. Overall, HPV-positive tumors consisted predominantly of NSCLC (28/29; 96.6%). HPV positivity according to histological subtype Although adenocarcinoma accounted for the largest number of HPV-positive tumors because it was the commonest histological subtype, the proportion of HPV positivity was higher in squamous cell carcinoma (Table 2, Figure 2). However, these differences were not statistically significant (p > 0.05). Clinicodemographic characteristics according to HPV status A comparison of clinicodemographic characteristics of patients with HPV positivity to those of the HPV-negative population is detailed in Table 3, in which age was presented only descriptively, and the Chi-square test was used to assess the significance of categorical data. Patients with HPV-positive tumors had a mean age of 64 years, compared with 60 years among HPV-negative patients. Male predominance was observed in both groups. Smoking was significantly associated with HPV positivity. Nearly 69% of HPV-positive patients were smokers compared with 45% among HPV-negative patients (p = 0.035). Most HPV-positive patients were residents of rural areas (65.5%), while 35% of them were from urban areas. Right-sided lung involvement was observed in 69% of HPV-positive patients compared with 59% of HPV-negative patients. Mortality was similar between the two groups. Discussion We conducted the current retrospective study to evaluate high-risk HPV infection in primary lung cancer using real-time PCR. We found that 30.5% of the retrieved specimens were positive for HPV-16, whereas HPV-18 was not detected in any specimen. HPV positivity was more frequent among smokers, patients with squamous cell carcinoma, and patients with right-sided tumors; however, only smoking was significantly associated with HPV positivity (p = 0.035). These results add to a growing body of evidence indicating that HPV-16 may be involved in pulmonary carcinogenesis among both smokers and nonsmokers, especially Asian patients. In the past three decades, infectious agents have also been studied as possible risk factors of lung carcinogenesis. High-risk HPV has drawn a lot of interest because its role as an oncogenic virus is well-established in cervical, anal, and oropharyngeal malignancies [3,5]. Nonetheless, the relationship between HPV and lung cancer remains controversial as a result of its striking geographical heterogeneity and inter-laboratory variability in testing techniques for the presence of virus components (morphology-based or molecular), along with differences in tissue-processing methods [13]. The prevalence of HPV-16 (30.5%) in the present study is higher than the global pooled estimate but is similar to that reported in recent meta-analyses from many Asian countries [10,14-16]. Geographic differences are well established, with HPV prevalence reported at less than 10% in studies from Europe and North America [14], even though higher detection rates have been reported in China [5], Taiwan [6], Japan, and some regions of India [9-16]. Such variation may reflect regional differences in HPV epidemiology, environmental exposures, and genetic susceptibility, as well as potential methodological contributors such as tissue preservation and DNA quality (e.g., PCR primers/target genes). Notably, HPV-18 was absent from all tumor samples. This finding was consistent with previous studies identifying HPV-16 as the most common genotype in malignant pulmonary carcinomas [11,17]. HPV-16 has a stronger oncogenic capacity than HPV-18 for squamous epithelial tissues and is also more frequently linked to extra-genital cancers. However, the absence of HPV-18 in this study should be interpreted with caution, as only two oncogenic genotypes were examined. A broader range of HPV genotyping using next-generation sequencing or multiplex PCR panels could uncover additional oncogenic HPVs implicated in lung carcinogenesis [18]. While adenocarcinoma was the most common histologic type in our cohort, squamous cell carcinoma had a higher proportion of HPV positivity. These data are in concordance with several previous studies [11,19]. Because viral replication is closely linked to epithelial differentiation, the squamous epithelium may be more vulnerable to persistent HPV infection. Histological subtype is important for determining prognosis and guiding subsequent management, as adenocarcinoma is associated with better survival than squamous cell carcinoma [20]. Additionally, HPV-induced dysregulation of the p53 and retinoblastoma pathways can promote malignant transformation in the squamous bronchial epithelium [5,13]. Conversely, a few other investigators have reported similar HPV prevalence across histological subtypes or found no significant association, suggesting that this relation remains unclear [8,21]. Therefore, larger multicenter studies sufficiently powered for histological subtypes are needed. Smoking is still the most significant established risk factor for lung cancer and was significantly associated with HPV positivity in this study. About two-thirds of HPV-positive patients had tobacco exposure. Cigarette smoke induces chronic epithelial injury, oxidative stress, DNA damage, and impairment of mucociliary clearance, which results in the development of persistent viral infection and local immune suppression [22]. Experimental evidence indicates that tobacco-related mutagens and carcinogens may interact with HPV oncoproteins to increase genomic instability [23] and promote malignant transformation. As a result, HPV infection might act as a cofactor rather than as an independent carcinogenic factor in susceptible hosts. An Iranian case-control study also reported a significant association between smoking and the risk of lung cancer (p < 0.05) [24]. However, the molecular and biological basis for HPV infection-induced lung carcinogenesis is not completely understood. High-risk HPV DNA is integrated into the host genome, resulting in persistent expression of the viral E6 and E7 oncoproteins, which promote p53 degradation and retinoblastoma protein inactivation, thereby stimulating cellular proliferation while inhibiting apoptosis [5-6]. Furthermore, activation of PI3K/Akt [25], EGFR, and Wnt/β-catenin signaling through HPV has also been linked to lung cancer development [13,26]. Chronic inflammation, cytokine dysregulation, and epigenetic changes resulting from persistent viral infection may also promote tumor development [27]. However, detection of HPV DNA alone does not establish active viral oncogenesis. More compelling evidence of biological relevance would include demonstration of viral integration, E6/E7 mRNA expression, or surrogate biomarkers such as p16 overexpression. While molecular studies and immunohistochemical testing have become part of lung cancer diagnosis, the IASLC recommendations still rely on expert consensus rather than mandating them for diagnosis and treatment [28]. Understanding the connection between HPV and lung cancer, in turn, will improve current knowledge of disease pathogenesis and identify potential prognostic or therapeutic responses through biomarker identification. While cancer vaccines have focused largely on host-derived neoantigens and tumor-associated antigens, HPV represents a distinct viral target in a subset of lung cancers. HPV-targeted vaccines remain largely unexplored for lung cancer, but preclinical studies suggest that vaccines targeting HPV E6 and E7 oncoproteins may enhance antitumor immunity in HPV-positive lung tumors [29]. papers.title: Clinicopathological Characteristics and Long-Term Outcomes After Conization for Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia Grade 2 (CIN2)
papers.abstract: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 (CIN2) represents a clinically heterogeneous condition with variable risks of persistence, regression, and progression. This study evaluated the clinicopathological characteristics and long-term outcomes of patients undergoing cervical conization for CIN2 and explored factors associated with residual or recurrent disease. A total of 195 patients treated between July 2016 and February 2026 were included. The median follow-up duration was 1.75 years (IQR, 0.83–5.04 years). Post-conization histology showed that 50.7% of cases were downgraded to CIN1 or normal, 35.8% persisted as CIN2, and 13.3% were upgraded to higher-grade lesions. Negative surgical margins were observed in 88.2% of patients. Findings suggestive of residual disease were identified in 26 patients during early follow-up, although histologically confirmed residual CIN2+ disease was observed in only three cases. During follow-up, nine patients developed findings suggestive for recurrence, whereas histologically confirmed recurrent CIN2+ disease was confirmed in three patients. HPV clearance was observed in 75% of patients with available follow-up testing. Multivariable analysis did not identify any independent predictors of relapse. These findings suggest that most CIN2 lesions regress or remain stable after conization, with low rates of histologically confirmed residual or recurrent high-grade disease, and highlight the limited predictive value of conventional clinicopathological factors in identifying patients at risk of relapse.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the clinicopathological characteristics and long-term outcomes of patients with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 (CIN2) after conization and to explore factors associated with residual or recurrent disease.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A total of 195 patients treated between July 2016 and February 2026 were included in the study. The median follow-up duration was 1.75 years (IQR, 0.83–5.04 years).
analysis.methods: The study used post-conization histology to assess lesion downgrades, persistence, and upgrades. It also evaluated surgical margins and follow-up findings for residual or recurrent disease.
analysis.main_results: Post-conization histology showed that 50.7% of cases were downgraded to CIN1 or normal, 35.8% persisted as CIN2, and 13.3% were upgraded to higher-grade lesions. analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide insights into the natural history of CIN2 following conization, which can inform clinical decision-making and surveillance strategies for HPV-associated cervical disease.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on histological confirmation for residual or recurrent disease, which may not capture all cases. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the study and potential for confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the clinicopathological characteristics and long-term outcomes of 195 patients with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 (CIN2) who underwent conization between 2016 and 2026. The median follow-up duration was 1.75 years. Post-conization histology revealed that 50.7% of cases were downgraded to CIN1 or normal, 35.8% persisted as CIN2, and 13.3% were upgraded to higher-grade lesions. Negative surgical margins were observed in 88.2% of patients. Early follow-up identified 26 patients with findings suggestive of residual disease, but only three had histologically confirmed residual CIN2+ disease. Nine patients showed findings suggestive of recurrence, with three confirmed to have recurrent CIN2+ disease. HPV clearance was noted in 75% of patients with follow-up testing. Multivariable analysis found no independent predictors of relapse. The authors concluded that most CIN2 lesions regress or remain stable after conization, with low rates of confirmed residual or recurrent high-grade disease, and emphasized the limited predictive value of conventional clinicopathological factors. The study's findings are of moderate evidence strength due to its observational design and potential for confounding factors.

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究依赖组织学确认残留或复发性疾病,可能无法涵盖所有病例,证据强度为中等,因研究为观察性设计且存在潜在混杂因素。

papers.title_zh: 宫颈上皮内瘤变2级(CIN2)锥切术后的临床病理特征及长期结局
papers.source_body_en: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 (CIN2) represents a clinically heterogeneous condition with variable risks of persistence, regression, and progression. This study evaluated the clinicopathological characteristics and long-term outcomes of patients undergoing cervical conization for CIN2 and explored factors associated with residual or recurrent disease. A total of 195 patients treated between July 2016 and February 2026 were included. The median follow-up duration was 1.75 years (IQR, 0.83–5.04 years). Post-conization histology showed that 50.7% of cases were downgraded to CIN1 or normal, 35.8% persisted as CIN2, and 13.3% were upgraded to higher-grade lesions. Negative surgical margins were observed in 88.2% of patients. Findings suggestive of residual disease were identified in 26 patients during early follow-up, although histologically confirmed residual CIN2+ disease was observed in only three cases. During follow-up, nine patients developed findings suggestive for recurrence, whereas histologically confirmed recurrent CIN2+ disease was confirmed in three patients. HPV clearance was observed in 75% of patients with available follow-up testing. Multivariable analysis did not identify any independent predictors of relapse. These findings suggest that most CIN2 lesions regress or remain stable after conization, with low rates of histologically confirmed residual or recurrent high-grade disease, and highlight the limited predictive value of conventional clinicopathological factors in identifying patients at risk of relapse.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估行宫颈锥切术治疗的宫颈上皮内瘤变2级(CIN2)患者的临床病理特征及长期结局,并探索与残留或复发性疾病相关的因素。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 研究共纳入2016年7月至2026年2月期间接受治疗的195名患者。中位随访时长为1.75年(四分位距,0.83–5.04年)。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究通过锥切术后组织学评估病变的降级、持续及进展情况,并评估手术切缘及随访发现以判断残留或复发性疾病。
analysis_zh.main_results: 锥切术后组织学显示,50.7%的病例降级至CIN1或正常,35.8%持续为CIN2,13.3%进展为高级别病变。88.2%的患者手术切缘为阴性。早期随访中,26例患者出现残留病变的影像学表现,但组织学确认的残留CIN2+病变仅3例。随访期间,9例患者出现复发的影像学表现,而组织学确认的复发性CIN2+病变仅3例。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果提示,大多数CIN2病变在锥切术后退行或保持稳定,高级别残留或复发性疾病的组织学确认率较低,并凸显常规临床病理因素在识别复发风险患者方面的有限预测价值。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为宫颈锥切术后CIN2的自然病程提供了见解,可为HPV相关宫颈疾病的临床决策及监测策略提供参考。

papers.title: Gynecologic cancers in low- and middle-income countries: Bridging the survival gap.
papers.abstract: Gynecologic malignancies-including cervical, endometrial, ovarian, vaginal, and vulvar cancers-represent a major and largely preventable source of mortality in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). In 2022, an estimated 1.47 million new cases and over 680,000 deaths were reported globally, with mortality disproportionately concentrated in resource-constrained settings. The survival gap between LMICs and high-income countries (HICs) remains profound, reflecting systemic policy and health system failures in prevention, early detection, and access to treatment. This narrative review synthesizes evidence from PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Library, and World Health Organization (WHO) databases, prioritizing literature published between January 2015 and December 2024, with a focus on epidemiology, health system constraints, and policy-relevant interventions. LMICs account for approximately 94% of global cervical cancer deaths, with the highest mortality observed in East Africa (age-standardized mortality rate 35.3 per 100,000). Persistent survival disparities are driven by late-stage diagnosis, limited screening coverage, inadequate radiotherapy infrastructure, workforce shortages, and restricted access to essential and novel therapies. However, evidence demonstrates that cost-effective and scalable interventions-including single-dose human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination, screen-and-treat strategies, HPV self-sampling, task-shifting models, and international training partnerships-can substantially improve outcomes when embedded within national cancer control policies and supported by sustainable financing mechanisms. Reducing these inequities requires policy-driven, system-level reforms that prioritize prevention, strengthen service delivery, and expand equitable access to care, aligning national strategies with global frameworks such as the WHO 90-70-90 targets to achieve sustainable cancer control in LMICs.

papers.title: HPV circulating tumor DNA as a potential prognostic and predictive biomarker in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Human papillomavirus circulating tumor DNA (HPVctDNA) has emerged as a promising prognostic biomarker in HPV-related head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). This systematic review aimed to synthesize current evidence on the diagnostic accuracy and prognostic value of HPVctDNA in HNSCC management. MATERIAL/METHODS: We systematically reviewed a PubMed-indexed database of studies published between January 2012 and September 2025. Eligible studies were assessed for design, primary tumor site and stage, treatment modality, HPVctDNA detection method, diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity and specificity), and reported clinical endpoints. Descriptive syntheses were performed; sensitivity and specificity were standardized to proportions and summarized as median values per group. RESULTS: A total of 60 studies, including 8,234 patients were analyzed, of which 41 (68.3%) focused exclusively on oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) and 17 (28.3%) included mixed HPV-related HNSCC subsites and HPV-positive cancers of unknown primary. The median follow-up across the included studies was 23 months. Among the included studies, 19 were retrospective (31.7%) and 33 were prospective (55.0%), with a small proportion of cross-sectional and randomized clinical trials. Overall, 40 (66.7%) evaluated the role of HPVctDNA in a curative setting. Plasma was the most common sample type, analyzed in 55 studies (91.7%), while 5 studies also included saliva. Detection methods varied: 40 employed droplet digital PCR (ddPCR), 16 used quantitative PCR (qPCR) and 4 applied NGS-based assays. Most of these studies (38, 63.3%) evaluated the prognostic utility of HPVctDNA, while only 4 (6.7%) assessed HPVctDNA in a screening or diagnostic setting. Regarding diagnostic accuracy, the median sensitivity across evaluable studies was 91.1%, while the median specificity was 99.4%. In OPSCC-only cohorts, the median sensitivity and specificity were 89.4% and 99.4%, respectively. Dynamic changes in HPVctDNA levels during or after treatment were consistently associated with outcomes: clearance or sustained negativity correlated with higher response rates, improved progression-free survival and overall survival, while persistent positivity or increasing levels predicted disease progression and recurrence. CONCLUSIONS: HPVctDNA demonstrates high diagnostic and prognostic accuracy in HPV-related HNSCC, especially OPSCC, supporting its use for prognosis, treatment monitoring and early detection of recurrence. However, prospective interventional studies are still required to demonstrate that HPVctDNA-guided treatment decisions improve clinical outcomes before routine implementation.

analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 总体而言,40项研究(66.7%)评估了HPVctDNA在根治性治疗情境中的作用。大多数研究(38项,63.3%)评估了HPVctDNA的预后价值,仅4项(6.7%)在筛查或诊断情境中评估HPVctDNA。在可评估研究中,中位敏感性为91.1%,中位特异性为99.4%。在仅限OPSCC的研究中,中位敏感性与特异性分别为89.4%与99.4%。HPVctDNA在HPV相关HNSCC(尤其是OPSCC)中展现出高诊断与预后准确性,支持其用于预后评估、治疗监测及早期复发检测。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 总共分析了 60 项研究,包括 8,234 名患者,其中 41 项 (68.3%) 专门针对口咽鳞状细胞癌 (OPSCC),17 项 (28.3%) 包括混合 HPV 相关 HNSCC 亚位点和原发灶不明的 HPV 阳性癌症。纳入研究的中位随访时间为 23 个月。纳入的研究中,回顾性研究19项(31.7%),前瞻性研究33项(55.0%),还有一小部分是横断面和随机临床试验。血浆是最常见的样本类型,有 55 项研究 (91.7%) 进行了分析,而 5 项研究还包括唾液。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 治疗 期间或之后 HPVctDNA 水平的动态变化始终与结果相关:清除或持续阴性与较高的缓解率、改善的无进展生存期和总生存期相关,而持续阳性或水平升高则预测疾病进展和复发。

papers.title: HPV-associated Anal Dysplasia in Solid Organ Transplant Recipients: A Transplant-specific Model of Mucosal Immune Dysfunction
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT: Solid organ transplant recipients face an increased risk of human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated anal cancer because of chronic immunosuppression and impaired viral control. The natural history and underlying biology of anal dysplasia in this population remain poorly defined, and current management is largely extrapolated from human immunodeficiency virus-associated disease. Transplant-related immune dysfunction differs fundamentally from other immunocompromised states, with direct effects on T-cell activation, antigen presentation, and immune memory that are central to HPV control. In this overview, we integrate insights from HPV-driven carcinogenesis, HIV-associated anal disease, and transplant immunology to propose a transplant-specific framework of mucosal immune dysfunction. In this model, HPV immune evasion synergizes chronic immunosuppression to impair antiviral cellular immunity, promoting persistent infection, and a protumorigenic microenvironment characterized by T-cell dysfunction, impaired antigen presentation, regulatory immune polarization, and metabolic reprogramming. These processes are hypothesized to facilitate progression to high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions, the immediate precursor to anal cancer. This framework provides a biologic basis to interpret clinically observed persistence and recurrence of anal dysplasia in solid organ transplant recipients, highlights key knowledge gaps and may inform transplant-specific screening, therapeutic strategies, and prospective studies in this high-risk population.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on the increased risk of HPV-associated anal cancer in solid organ transplant recipients due to chronic immunosuppression and impaired viral control. It highlights the unique immune dysfunction in transplant patients, which differs from other immunocompromised states, and emphasizes the role of T-cell activation, antigen presentation, and immune memory in HPV control. The study proposes a transplant-specific framework for understanding mucosal immune dysfunction and its implications for the progression of anal dysplasia to high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions. The review also identifies key knowledge gaps and suggests the need for transplant-specific screening and therapeutic strategies.

papers.title_zh: 实体器官移植受者中人乳头瘤病毒相关性肛门发育异常:一种黏膜免疫功能障碍的移植特异性模型
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT: Solid organ transplant recipients face an increased risk of human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated anal cancer because of chronic immunosuppression and impaired viral control. The natural history and underlying biology of anal dysplasia in this population remain poorly defined, and current management is largely extrapolated from human immunodeficiency virus-associated disease. Transplant-related immune dysfunction differs fundamentally from other immunocompromised states, with direct effects on T-cell activation, antigen presentation, and immune memory that are central to HPV control. In this overview, we integrate insights from HPV-driven carcinogenesis, HIV-associated anal disease, and transplant immunology to propose a transplant-specific framework of mucosal immune dysfunction. In this model, HPV immune evasion synergizes chronic immunosuppression to impair antiviral cellular immunity, promoting persistent infection, and a protumorigenic microenvironment characterized by T-cell dysfunction, impaired antigen presentation, regulatory immune polarization, and metabolic reprogramming. These processes are hypothesized to facilitate progression to high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions, the immediate precursor to anal cancer. This framework provides a biologic basis to interpret clinically observed persistence and recurrence of anal dysplasia in solid organ transplant recipients, highlights key knowledge gaps and may inform transplant-specific screening, therapeutic strategies, and prospective studies in this high-risk population.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要:由于慢性免疫抑制和病毒控制受损,实体器官移植受者患 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 相关肛门癌的风险增加。该人群肛门发育不良的自然史和基础生物学仍不清楚,目前的治疗很大程度上是从人类免疫缺陷病毒相关疾病中推断出来的。移植相关的免疫功能障碍与其他免疫功能低下状态有根本不同,它直接影响对 HPV 控制至关重要的 T 细胞激活、抗原呈递和免疫记忆。在本概述中,我们整合了 HPV 驱动的致癌作用、HIV 相关肛门疾病和移植免疫学的见解,提出了粘膜免疫功能障碍的移植特异性框架。在该模型中,HPV 免疫逃避协同慢性免疫抑制,损害 抗病毒药物 细胞免疫,促进持续感染,以及以 T 细胞功能障碍、抗原呈递受损、调节性免疫极化和代谢重编程为特征的促肿瘤微环境。假设这些过程促进高级鳞状上皮内病变的进展,这是肛门癌的直接前兆。该框架为解释临床观察到的实体器官移植受者肛门发育不良的持续性和复发提供了生物学基础,强调了关键的知识差距,并可能为这一高危人群的移植特异性筛查、治疗策略和前瞻性研究提供信息。

papers.title: HPV-associated Oropharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: An Imaging Framework for AJCC Version 9 TNM Staging
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) is biologically and prognostically distinct from HPV-negative disease, and staging directly impacts treatment. The American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) and Union for International Cancer Control version 9 TNM staging system incorporates unequivocal imaging-detected and/or clinically detected extranodal extension (iENE) into clinical nodal staging and definitive pathologic extranodal extension into pathologic nodal staging. Additionally, it provides more explicit anatomic definitions for advanced local disease (clinical T4) while maintaining T and M category definitions from the eighth edition. Radiologists play a central role in the multidisciplinary team by evaluating endophytic tumor extent, regional nodal disease and iENE, and distant metastasis using CT, MRI, and PET. This article reviews clinically relevant oropharyngeal anatomy and proposes a practical radiologic approach to assigning T, N, and M categories in HPV-associated OPSCC. It emphasizes cautious interpretation of iENE because of interreader variability and imperfect diagnostic performance, with further high-grade evidence needed to establish its consistently reproducible, incremental prognostic value as a clinical N category modifier. It also highlights multidisciplinary factors that guide selection of surgical resection versus nonsurgical therapy. Posttreatment evaluation is discussed in the context of blood-based biomarkers such as tumor tissue-modified viral HPV DNA. The goal of this article is to provide a practical, staging-focused imaging framework for evaluation of HPV-associated OPSCC. Keywords: CT, MR Imaging, Head/Neck, Neck, Pharynx, Surgery, Human Papillomavirus, Squamous Cell Carcinoma, Oropharynx, Transoral Robotic Surgery, Oropharyngeal Carcinoma, TTMV HPV DNA © RSNA, 2026.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC), focusing on the role of imaging in TNM staging under the AJCC version 9 system, specifically addressing how staging impacts treatment decisions for HPV-positive disease.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The article is a narrative review that outlines the AJCC and UICC version 9 TNM staging criteria for HPV-associated OPSCC, emphasizing imaging-based evaluation of tumor extent, nodal disease, and extranodal extension (iENE) using CT, MRI, and PET.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review agrees that HPV-associated OPSCC is biologically and prognostically distinct from HPV-negative disease, with staging directly influencing treatment choices; it also concludes that AJCC version 9 incorporates iENE into nodal staging and maintains T and M category definitions from the eighth edition.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is uncertainty regarding the consistent reproducibility and incremental prognostic value of imaging-detected extranodal extension (iENE) due to interreader variability and imperfect diagnostic performance, necessitating higher-grade evidence to validate its role as a clinical N category modifier.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review highlights the need for further high-grade evidence to establish the prognostic utility of iENE and calls for cautious interpretation in clinical practice; it also emphasizes the importance of multidisciplinary collaboration in selecting between surgical resection and nonsurgical therapy.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) and its imaging-based TNM staging under the AJCC version 9 system. It underscores the biological and prognostic distinctiveness of HPV-positive OPSCC compared to HPV-negative disease, with staging directly influencing treatment decisions. The AJCC version 9 incorporates imaging-detected extranodal extension (iENE) into nodal staging while retaining T and M category definitions from the eighth edition. Radiologists play a central role in evaluating tumor extent, nodal disease, and iENE using CT, MRI, and PET. However, the reproducibility and prognostic value of iENE remain uncertain due to interreader variability and diagnostic limitations, requiring higher-grade evidence. The review also stresses multidisciplinary factors in selecting between surgical and nonsurgical therapies and calls for further research to validate iENE's clinical utility.

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review examines HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC), focusing on the role of imaging in TNM staging under the AJCC version 9 system, specifically addressing how staging impacts treatment decisions for HPV-positive disease.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The article is a narrative review that outlines the AJCC and UICC version 9 TNM staging criteria for HPV-associated OPSCC, emphasizing imaging-based evaluation of tumor extent, nodal disease, and extranodal extension (iENE) using CT, MRI, and PET.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review agrees that HPV-associated OPSCC is biologically and prognostically distinct from HPV-negative disease, with staging directly influencing treatment choices; it also concludes that AJCC version 9 incorporates iENE into nodal staging and maintains T and M category definitions from the eighth edition.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is uncertainty regarding the consistent reproducibility and incremental prognostic value of imaging-detected extranodal extension (iENE) due to interreader variability and imperfect diagnostic performance, necessitating higher-grade evidence to validate its role as a clinical N category modifier.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review highlights the need for further high-grade evidence to establish the prognostic utility of iENE and calls for cautious interpretation in clinical practice; it also emphasizes the importance of multidisciplinary collaboration in selecting between surgical resection and nonsurgical therapy.

papers.source_body_en: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) is biologically and prognostically distinct from HPV-negative disease, and staging directly impacts treatment. The American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) and Union for International Cancer Control version 9 TNM staging system incorporates unequivocal imaging-detected and/or clinically detected extranodal extension (iENE) into clinical nodal staging and definitive pathologic extranodal extension into pathologic nodal staging. Additionally, it provides more explicit anatomic definitions for advanced local disease (clinical T4) while maintaining T and M category definitions from the eighth edition. Radiologists play a central role in the multidisciplinary team by evaluating endophytic tumor extent, regional nodal disease and iENE, and distant metastasis using CT, MRI, and PET. This article reviews clinically relevant oropharyngeal anatomy and proposes a practical radiologic approach to assigning T, N, and M categories in HPV-associated OPSCC. It emphasizes cautious interpretation of iENE because of interreader variability and imperfect diagnostic performance, with further high-grade evidence needed to establish its consistently reproducible, incremental prognostic value as a clinical N category modifier. It also highlights multidisciplinary factors that guide selection of surgical resection versus nonsurgical therapy. Posttreatment evaluation is discussed in the context of blood-based biomarkers such as tumor tissue-modified viral HPV DNA. The goal of this article is to provide a practical, staging-focused imaging framework for evaluation of HPV-associated OPSCC. papers.title: Efficacy of mRNA-based HPV Vaccines in Inducing Immune Response and Preventing Oncogenic Outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection represents a substantial global health burden, being the primary etiological agent of cervical cancer, anogenital and oropharyngeal malignancies. Although prophylactic virus-like particle (VLP) vaccines have been successfully implemented, they lack therapeutic efficacy against established infections and lesions in the host. The messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccine platform has emerged as a promising alternative, offering rapid manufacturing and the ability to induce potent cellular immune responses required for effective therapeutic outcomes. Objective This systematic review aimed to synthesize and evaluate preclinical evidence regarding the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of mRNA-based HPV vaccines in animal models, focusing on their ability to prevent oncogenic infections and induce regression of established tumors. Methods The study is registered in Prospero (CRD420261362037, 14 July 2026). A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Europe PMC, and ScienceDirect databases was conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Eligible studies included in vivo preclinical experimental research evaluating mRNA vaccines targeting high-risk HPV types (HPV-16 and HPV-18) in animal models. Immunogenicity (CD8+ T-cell responses and IgG titers) and oncogenic outcome (tumor volume and survival rate) data were extracted. The risk of bias was assessed using the SYRCLE’s risk-of-bias tool. The meta-analysis utilized a random-effects model to calculate standardized mean differences (SMD) and evaluate heterogeneity via the I 2 statistic. Result and Conclusion Ten studies met the inclusion criteria and provided detailed data for the analysis. mRNA vaccines have demonstrated high immunogenicity, significantly expanding antigen-specific CD8+ T-cell populations and inducing robust IFN gamma secretion. The pooled results indicated a significant reduction in tumor volume (SMD -2.305; 95% CI: −2.64 to −1.97) and near-complete viral load reduction in the challenge models. High-risk HPV mRNA vaccines delivered via lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) or lipopolyplexes (LPPs) have a promising therapeutic potential as both prophylactic and therapeutic agents, supporting their advancement to clinical trials.

papers.title_original: Efficacy of mRNA-based HPV Vaccines in Inducing Immune Response and Preventing Oncogenic Outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human papillomaviruses (HPV), focusing on high-risk types (e.g., HPV-16, HPV-18) and their association with oncogenic outcomes such as cervical, anogenital, and oropharyngeal malignancies, as well as HPV infection and genital warts in the host. The central question evaluates the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of mRNA-based HPV vaccines in preclinical animal models, specifically their ability to prevent oncogenic infections and induce regression of established tumors.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This systematic review and meta-analysis is registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261362037, 14 July 2026) and follows PRISMA 2020 guidelines. A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Europe PMC, and ScienceDirect. Eligible studies included in vivo preclinical experimental research evaluating mRNA vaccines targeting high-risk HPV types (HPV-16 and HPV-18) in animal models. Immunogenicity (CD8+ T-cell responses and IgG titers) and oncogenic outcome (tumor volume and survival rate) data were extracted. The risk of bias was assessed using SYRCLE’s tool, and a random-effects meta-analysis calculated standardized mean differences (SMD) with heterogeneity evaluated via the I2 statistic.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The pooled results demonstrate that mRNA vaccines induce high immunogenicity, significantly expanding antigen-specific CD8+ T-cell populations and inducing robust IFN gamma secretion. There is a significant reduction in tumor volume (SMD -2.305; 95% CI: −2.64 to −1.97) and near-complete viral load reduction in challenge models. High-risk HPV mRNA vaccines delivered via lipid nanoparticles or lipopolyplexes show promising therapeutic potential as both prophylactic and therapeutic agents.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report long-term safety data, durability of immune responses, or comparative efficacy against established prophylactic virus-like particle (VLP) vaccines in humans. Additionally, the evidence base is limited to preclinical animal models, leaving uncertainties about translational potential to human clinical settings.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings support the advancement of mRNA-based HPV vaccines to clinical trials, particularly for therapeutic applications against established infections and lesions. Priority research areas include evaluating long-term safety, durability of immune responses, and comparative efficacy in human populations. Surveillance and diagnostic strategies should incorporate immunogenicity and tumor regression metrics to monitor vaccine performance in clinical trials.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of mRNA-based HPV vaccines in preclinical animal models, focusing on high-risk HPV types (HPV-16 and HPV-18). The review synthesizes evidence from ten preclinical studies, demonstrating that mRNA vaccines induce robust CD8+ T-cell responses, IFN gamma secretion, and significant reductions in tumor volume and viral load. The pooled results support the therapeutic potential of mRNA vaccines delivered via lipid nanoparticles or lipopolyplexes, warranting advancement to clinical trials. However, the evidence is limited to preclinical models, with gaps in long-term safety, durability of immune responses, and comparative efficacy against established VLP vaccines. The review highlights the need for clinical trials to validate these findings and inform future vaccination strategies.

Although prophylactic virus-like particle (VLP) vaccines have been successfully implemented, they lack therapeutic efficacy against established infections and lesions in the host. Methods The study is registered in Prospero (CRD420261362037, 14 July 2026). A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Europe PMC, and ScienceDirect databases was conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Eligible studies included in vivo preclinical experimental research evaluating mRNA vaccines targeting high-risk HPV types (HPV-16 and HPV-18) in animal models. High-risk HPV mRNA vaccines delivered via lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) or lipopolyplexes (LPPs) have a promising therapeutic potential as both prophylactic and therapeutic agents, supporting their advancement to clinical trials.

papers.title: Integrating non-coding RNA profiling with HPV genotyping for cervical cancer risk stratification and early detection
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer is a major global health concern and a leading cause of cancer-related deaths among women worldwide. Although current diagnostic methods have improved diagnosis but are limited in distinguishing transient infections from those progressing toward malignancy. This limitation highlights the need for more precise diagnostic approaches that can support early intervention, risk assessment, and informed clinical decision-making. HPV genotyping includes identification of specific high-risk viral strains, providing essential information for infection risk assessment, disease surveillance, and vaccine evaluation. However, it does not indicate viral oncogenic activity or cellular transformation. On the other hand, ncRNAs such as miRNAs, lncRNAs, and circRNAs serve as key regulatory molecules in HPV-mediated carcinogenesis. Moreover, their stability in biological fluids supports their use as non-invasive, liquid biopsy-based diagnostics. This narrative review explores the potential of integrating HPV genotyping with ncRNA profiling as a multi-omics diagnostic approach for cervical cancer risk stratification. By combining information on viral genotype with host molecular responses, this integrated strategy may improve diagnostic accuracy, enhance patient risk stratification, and facilitate more personalized screening and management. Although individual ncRNA biomarkers have shown promising associations with HPV-associated cervical carcinogenesis, evidence supporting their combined clinical application with HPV genotyping remains limited and requires further prospective validation. Nevertheless, the integration of viral and host molecular biomarkers represents a potentially useful approach for improving molecular risk assessment and supporting the development of more personalized cervical cancer screening strategies.

papers.title: HPV Knowledge, Anxiety and Vaccine Acceptance Among Adults in Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) causes various infections and serious health complications, including cancer. Vaccine hesitancy and anxiety continue to hinder its control. This study assessed HPV-related knowledge, infection anxiety, and vaccine hesitancy among the adult population in Saudi Arabia (including both citizens and non-Saudi residents), as well as exposure to skin and genital warts. A total of 2014 adults (≥ 18 years) completed an online survey covering demographics, HPV knowledge, and the modified Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) scale adapted to measure HPV-specific concerns. Skin warts were common, particularly among females aged 21-50 years, whereas genital warts were less frequent, peaking in the 21-40 age group. Anxiety was highest among participants aged 18-30 years. Notable knowledge gaps existed regarding HPV transmission and vaccine benefits. Younger participants showed better understanding, but males were less aware of vaccine availability. Healthcare professionals and medical students demonstrated superior knowledge. Multinomial logistic regression showed that gender was the only significant predictor of vaccine willingness (p < 0.001). Males were more likely than females to say "yes" (aOR = 1.409, p = 0.009) and "no" (aOR = 1.633, p < 0.001), indicating that females were disproportionately hesitant ("not sure"). A high school education (vs. a medical background) was associated with lower willingness (aOR = 0.631, p = 0.030). Overall, the findings emphasize the need for targeted educational campaigns to improve HPV awareness and promote vaccine acceptance.

papers.title_original: HPV Knowledge, Anxiety and Vaccine Acceptance Among Adults in Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human papillomaviruses (HPV), their associated diseases (including cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and HPV-associated cancers), and vaccine hesitancy among adults in Saudi Arabia, focusing on knowledge gaps, infection anxiety, and determinants of vaccine acceptance.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review synthesizes cross-sectional survey data from 2014 adults (≥18 years) in Saudi Arabia, including demographics, HPV knowledge assessments, and HPV-specific anxiety measured via a modified Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) scale. It employs multinomial logistic regression to identify predictors of vaccine willingness.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Younger participants demonstrated better HPV knowledge, while males exhibited lower awareness of vaccine availability and higher hesitancy. Healthcare professionals and medical students had superior knowledge. Gender was the only significant predictor of vaccine willingness (p < 0.001), with males more likely to accept or refuse vaccination compared to females.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Knowledge gaps persisted regarding HPV transmission and vaccine benefits, particularly among non-medical backgrounds. The study did not address regional disparities, cultural barriers, or long-term behavioral outcomes post-intervention. Anxiety levels were highest in the 18-30 age group, but causal links to vaccine hesitancy were not established.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Targeted educational campaigns are needed to improve HPV awareness, particularly among males and non-medical populations. Surveillance should monitor vaccine acceptance trends and address misconceptions about HPV transmission and vaccine efficacy. Further research is required to evaluate the impact of anxiety on vaccine uptake and to design culturally tailored interventions.

analysis.summary_en: This review synthesizes evidence on HPV-related knowledge, anxiety, and vaccine hesitancy among adults in Saudi Arabia. A cross-sectional survey of 2014 participants revealed significant knowledge gaps, particularly regarding HPV transmission and vaccine benefits, with males and non-medical backgrounds showing lower awareness. Younger participants and those in healthcare fields demonstrated better understanding. Gender was the sole significant predictor of vaccine willingness, with males more likely to accept or refuse vaccination. Anxiety was highest among 18-30-year-olds, but its causal relationship to hesitancy remains unclear. The findings underscore the need for targeted educational interventions to address misconceptions and improve vaccine acceptance.

elements_en.scope_and_question: The review examines human papillomaviruses (HPV), their associated diseases (including cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and HPV-associated cancers), and vaccine hesitancy among adults in Saudi Arabia, focusing on knowledge gaps, infection anxiety, and determinants of vaccine acceptance.

elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Younger participants demonstrated better HPV knowledge, while males exhibited lower awareness of vaccine availability and higher hesitancy. elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Knowledge gaps persisted regarding HPV transmission and vaccine benefits, particularly among non-medical backgrounds. elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: Targeted educational campaigns are needed to improve HPV awareness, particularly among males and non-medical populations. papers.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯成年人的 HPV 知识、焦虑和 疫苗 接受度:一项横断面研究。
papers.source_body_en: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) causes various infections and serious health complications, including cancer. Vaccine hesitancy and anxiety continue to hinder its control. This study assessed HPV-related knowledge, infection anxiety, and vaccine hesitancy among the adult population in Saudi Arabia (including both citizens and non-Saudi residents), as well as exposure to skin and genital warts. A total of 2014 adults (≥ 18 years) completed an online survey covering demographics, HPV knowledge, and the modified Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) scale adapted to measure HPV-specific concerns. Skin warts were common, particularly among females aged 21-50 years, whereas genital warts were less frequent, peaking in the 21-40 age group. Anxiety was highest among participants aged 18-30 years. Notable knowledge gaps existed regarding HPV transmission and vaccine benefits. Younger participants showed better understanding, but males were less aware of vaccine availability. Healthcare professionals and medical students demonstrated superior knowledge. Multinomial logistic regression showed that gender was the only significant predictor of vaccine willingness (p < 0.001). Males were more likely than females to say "yes" (aOR = 1.409, p = 0.009) and "no" (aOR = 1.633, p < 0.001), indicating that females were disproportionately hesitant ("not sure"). A high school education (vs. a medical background) was associated with lower willingness (aOR = 0.631, p = 0.030). Overall, the findings emphasize the need for targeted educational campaigns to improve HPV awareness and promote vaccine acceptance.
papers.abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 会导致各种感染和严重的健康并发症,包括癌症。疫苗的犹豫和焦虑继续阻碍着它的控制。本研究评估了沙特阿拉伯成年人群(包括公民和非沙特居民)的 HPV 相关知识、感染焦虑和 疫苗 犹豫度,以及接触皮肤和生殖器疣的情况。共有 2014 名成年人(≥ 18 岁)完成了一项在线调查,内容涵盖人口统计、HPV 知识以及适用于衡量 HPV 特定问题的改良版广泛性焦虑症 7 (GAD-7) 量表。皮肤疣很常见,特别是在 21-50 岁的女性中,而生殖器疣则较少见,在 21-40 岁年龄组中达到高峰。18-30 岁参与者的焦虑程度最高。关于 HPV 传播 和 疫苗 益处存在显着的知识差距。年轻的参与者表现出更好的理解力,但男性不太了解 疫苗 的可用性。医疗保健专业人员和医学生展示了卓越的知识。多项 Logistic 回归显示,性别是 疫苗 意愿的唯一显着预测因子 (p < 0.001)。男性比女性更有可能说“是”(aOR = 1.409,p = 0.009)和“否”(aOR = 1.633,p < 0.001),这表明女性不成比例地犹豫(“不确定”)。高中教育(相对于医学背景)与较低的意愿相关(aOR = 0.631,p = 0.030)。总体而言,研究结果强调需要开展有针对性的教育活动,以提高 HPV 意识并促进 疫苗 的接受。

papers.title: Penile Intraepithelial Neoplasia and Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Contemporary Review of Clinicopathologic Features, Classification, and Prognostication.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Penile intraepithelial neoplasia is an uncommon precancerous genital lesion that may progress to invasive penile squamous cell carcinoma in the absence of proper therapeutic management. The recent trend of increasing incidence because of a heightened burden of genital human papillomavirus (HPV) infection emphasizes a need for effective diagnostic and management strategies. This article provides a clinicopathologic overview focusing on updates in tumor classification and prognostication not previously summarized. We examine changes in classification and nomenclature based on the 2022 World Health Organization guidelines and explore differences in pathogenesis and prognosis between HPV-associated and HPV-independent tumors. This article emphasizes the need for more robust molecular genetic studies to further elucidate prognostic biomarkers and explores the increasingly distinct role of immunohistochemistry in stratifying subtypes. Also, we present an illustrative case to highlight the significance of accurate diagnosis and prompt management.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human papillomaviruses (HPV) and their association with penile intraepithelial neoplasia (PeIN) and penile squamous cell carcinoma (PSCC), focusing on the central question of how HPV-driven pathogenesis and classification updates inform diagnostic and prognostic strategies for these HPV-associated genital lesions.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a contemporary clinicopathologic overview summarizing updates in tumor classification and prognostication based on the 2022 World Health Organization guidelines, with a focus on distinguishing HPV-associated from HPV-independent penile tumors.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that penile intraepithelial neoplasia is a precancerous lesion with potential progression to invasive penile squamous cell carcinoma without proper management, and emphasizes the increasing incidence of HPV-associated penile lesions due to rising genital HPV infection burden.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies a need for more robust molecular genetic studies to elucidate prognostic biomarkers and to clarify the distinct roles of immunohistochemistry in stratifying HPV-associated versus HPV-independent penile tumor subtypes.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review underscores the importance of accurate diagnosis and prompt management of penile intraepithelial neoplasia to prevent progression to invasive carcinoma, and calls for improved diagnostic and management strategies in the context of rising HPV-associated disease incidence.

analysis.summary_en: This review synthesizes contemporary evidence on human papillomaviruses (HPV) and their association with penile intraepithelial neoplasia (PeIN) and penile squamous cell carcinoma (PSCC). It centers on how HPV-driven pathogenesis and updated classification systems inform diagnostic and prognostic approaches. The review confirms that PeIN is a precancerous lesion with progression risk to invasive PSCC without treatment, and notes a rising incidence of HPV-associated penile lesions linked to increased genital HPV burden. Key gaps include the need for stronger molecular studies to identify prognostic biomarkers and refine immunohistochemistry-based stratification of HPV-associated versus HPV-independent tumors. The review emphasizes accurate diagnosis and timely intervention to mitigate progression risk.

papers.title_zh: 阴茎上皮内瘤变和鳞状细胞癌:临床病理特征、分类和预后的当代回顾。
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Penile intraepithelial neoplasia is an uncommon precancerous genital lesion that may progress to invasive penile squamous cell carcinoma in the absence of proper therapeutic management. The recent trend of increasing incidence because of a heightened burden of genital human papillomavirus (HPV) infection emphasizes a need for effective diagnostic and management strategies. This article provides a clinicopathologic overview focusing on updates in tumor classification and prognostication not previously summarized. We examine changes in classification and nomenclature based on the 2022 World Health Organization guidelines and explore differences in pathogenesis and prognosis between HPV-associated and HPV-independent tumors. This article emphasizes the need for more robust molecular genetic studies to further elucidate prognostic biomarkers and explores the increasingly distinct role of immunohistochemistry in stratifying subtypes. Also, we present an illustrative case to highlight the significance of accurate diagnosis and prompt management.

papers.title: Society for Maternal‐Fetal Medicine Special Statement: Reducing the risk of transmitting infection during ultrasound examination—Updated 2026
papers.abstract: Abstract Ultrasound examinations have the potential to transmit infections between individuals. The risk can be reduced by following certain well‐described procedures to clean and disinfect ultrasound transducers between examinations. However, surveys have shown widespread lapses in the cleaning and disinfection of transducers and other equipment. In 2020, the Society for Maternal‐Fetal Medicine (SMFM) published a Patient Safety Guideline focused on reducing the risk of transmitting infection in transvaginal examinations, with emphasis on selection of high‐level disinfectants with proven efficacy against human papillomavirus (HPV), choice of transducer covers with documented low leakage rates, and cautions regarding multiuse containers of coupling gel. In this article, SMFM presents updated guidelines with an expanded scope that includes transabdominal examinations and ultrasound‐guided percutaneous and intraoperative procedures. Other updates include a list of newer high‐level disinfection systems and citation of recent literature on virucidal efficacy of ortho‐phthalaldehyde against HPV. The guidelines are based on the Spaulding classification of infection risk and are aligned with recommendations from the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and the US Food and Drug Administration. This Special Statement replaces Society for Maternal‐Fetal Medicine Special Statement: Reducing the risk of transmitting infection by transvaginal ultrasound examination, 2020 .

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on human papillomaviruses (HPV), specifically high-risk HPV types such as HPV16, HPV18, HPV31, HPV33, HPV45, HPV52, and HPV58, and their association with diseases like cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, HPV-associated cervical cancer, HPV-associated anal cancer, HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer, genital warts, and anogenital warts. The central question is how to reduce the risk of transmitting HPV during ultrasound examinations, particularly transvaginal, transabdominal, and ultrasound-guided procedures.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is an updated guideline from the Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine (SMFM) that incorporates recent literature and new disinfection systems. It references the Spaulding classification of infection risk and aligns with recommendations from the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and the US Food and Drug Administration. The review includes surveys highlighting lapses in cleaning and disinfection practices.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that the risk of transmitting HPV during ultrasound examinations can be reduced by following procedures to clean and disinfect ultrasound transducers between uses. It emphasizes the use of high-level disinfectants with proven efficacy against HPV, particularly ortho-phthalaldehyde, and the importance of transducer covers with low leakage rates. The guidelines also caution against the use of multiuse containers of coupling gel.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that surveys have shown widespread lapses in the cleaning and disinfection of transducers and other equipment, indicating a gap in adherence to recommended practices. There is no explicit mention of controversies, but the lack of consistent implementation suggests unresolved issues in practice.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review recommends updating disinfection protocols, using newer high-level disinfection systems, and ensuring proper training for healthcare providers to prevent HPV transmission during ultrasound procedures. It also highlights the need for ongoing surveillance and adherence to guidelines to reduce infection risks.

analysis.summary_en: This review updates guidelines for reducing the risk of transmitting human papillomaviruses (HPV) during ultrasound examinations, including transvaginal, transabdominal, and ultrasound-guided procedures. It emphasizes the importance of cleaning and disinfecting transducers with high-level disinfectants proven effective against HPV, such as ortho-phthalaldehyde, and the use of transducer covers with low leakage rates. The review highlights widespread lapses in adherence to these practices and aligns with recommendations from multiple authoritative bodies. The guidelines aim to improve infection control through updated protocols and provider training.

papers.title_zh: 母胎医学学会特别声明:降低超声检查期间感染传播风险——2026年更新
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Ultrasound examinations have the potential to transmit infections between individuals. The risk can be reduced by following certain well‐described procedures to clean and disinfect ultrasound transducers between examinations. However, surveys have shown widespread lapses in the cleaning and disinfection of transducers and other equipment. In 2020, the Society for Maternal‐Fetal Medicine (SMFM) published a Patient Safety Guideline focused on reducing the risk of transmitting infection in transvaginal examinations, with emphasis on selection of high‐level disinfectants with proven efficacy against human papillomavirus (HPV), choice of transducer covers with documented low leakage rates, and cautions regarding multiuse containers of coupling gel. In this article, SMFM presents updated guidelines with an expanded scope that includes transabdominal examinations and ultrasound‐guided percutaneous and intraoperative procedures. Other updates include a list of newer high‐level disinfection systems and citation of recent literature on virucidal efficacy of ortho‐phthalaldehyde against HPV. The guidelines are based on the Spaulding classification of infection risk and are aligned with recommendations from the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and the US Food and Drug Administration. This Special Statement replaces Society for Maternal‐Fetal Medicine Special Statement: Reducing the risk of transmitting infection by transvaginal ultrasound examination, 2020 .

papers.title: Application of Cobas 6800 HPV testing and qPCR utilizing three genomically-optimized primer sets for detecting HPV DNA in the blood of HPV Positive dysplasia and cancer patients
papers.abstract: Use of quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) to measure viral DNA in plasma has promise for the detection and/or monitoring of high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV)-associated cancers. We examined Roche’s cobas 6800 HPV test for detection of hrHPV in plasma or peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) of patients with HPV-associated dysplasia or cancer. In our pilot study, this assay detected hrHPV DNA in 1 mL pre-treatment plasma of patients with advanced (stage II-IV) cervical cancer, but not stage I or dysplasia cases, or in PBMC. Plasma of oropharyngeal cancer patients also tested positive in most cases. Seeking to enhance sensitivity, we re-tested these pilot samples with qPCR employing three published primer sets (E7, BR E1-5, HR E5L2-4) selected for improved detection of HPV16 in cancer. This triplex assay detected quantifiable levels of HPV16 in pre-treatment plasma of advanced (stage II-IV) cervical cancer cases, and lower levels in some stage I and dysplasia cases. In serial sampling of HPV16 + cervical cancer patients post-treatment with no evidence of disease over ~2 years, no reproducible signal was detected by cobas HPV testing, whereas the triplex qPCR sporadically detected HPV DNA in plasma and PBMC samples of a subset of these patients.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the utility of qPCR for detecting HPV DNA in plasma and to explore its potential for monitoring hrHPV-associated cancers.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A pilot study was conducted using pre-treatment plasma samples from patients with advanced cervical cancer, stage I cervical cancer, and HPV-associated dysplasia, as well as oropharyngeal cancer patients.
analysis.methods: The study employed Roche’s cobas 6800 HPV test and triplex qPCR with three genomically-optimized primer sets (E7, BR E1-5, HR E5L2-4) to detect HPV16 and other hrHPV types in plasma samples.
analysis.main_results: The cobas HPV test detected hrHPV DNA in advanced cervical cancer plasma but not in stage I or dysplasia cases or PBMC. The triplex qPCR detected quantifiable HPV16 levels in advanced cervical cancer plasma and lower levels in some stage I and dysplasia cases. Post-treatment serial sampling showed no reproducible signal with cobas testing, but sporadic HPV DNA detection was observed in a subset of patients using triplex qPCR.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The triplex qPCR demonstrated improved sensitivity for detecting HPV16 in plasma compared to the cobas test, suggesting its potential for more accurate monitoring of HPV-associated cancers.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform the development of more sensitive diagnostic tools for HPV-associated cancers, particularly in plasma-based detection, which could enhance surveillance and monitoring strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to a pilot sample size and focused on HPV16, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is moderate due to the exploratory nature of the study and the lack of long-term follow-up data.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the use of qPCR with three genomically-optimized primer sets for detecting HPV DNA in plasma from patients with HPV-associated dysplasia and cancer. The cobas 6800 HPV test detected hrHPV in advanced cervical cancer plasma but not in stage I or dysplasia cases or PBMC. The triplex qPCR showed improved sensitivity for HPV16 detection in plasma and some stage I and dysplasia cases. Post-treatment serial sampling revealed no reproducible signal with cobas testing, but sporadic HPV DNA detection was observed in a subset of patients using triplex qPCR. The triplex qPCR demonstrated potential for more accurate monitoring of HPV-associated cancers, which could inform improved diagnostic strategies. However, the study's limited sample size and focus on HPV16 may restrict its generalizability, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于试点样本量,并重点关注 HPV16,这可能会影响普遍性。由于该研究的探索性和缺乏长期随访数据,证据是中等的。

papers.title: Immunological consequences of mesenchymal stem cell therapy in HPV-driven cervical cancer: a systematic review and stratification framework.
papers.abstract: Over 660,000 women develop cervical cancer annually, caused by persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV). Published studies of mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs) as immunomodulatory agents are contradictory, with some reporting tumor suppression and others tumor promotion. The mechanism of these paradoxes has not been systematically investigated. This review aims to assess MSC-mediated immune evasion in HPV-related cervical cancer, quantify HPV stratification failure in the literature, and formulate a predictive stratification model linking MSC behavior to HPV oncogenic activity. A systematic review was performed following PRISMA 2020 guidelines across 8 databases. Studies were included if they reported an MSC intervention for cervical cancer with one or more immune-related outcomes. HPV stratification gap analysis was performed alongside data extraction and risk-of-bias evaluation. 14 studies were included: 13 completed preclinical and 1 ongoing clinical trial. MSC effects included immune evasion through adenosine, IL-10, and M2 macrophage polarization, and tumor suppression through STAT3, Wnt/β-Catenin, and epigenetic pathways. Of 13 completed studies, none measured HPV oncogenic activity as an experimental variable. Only two included an HPV-negative cohort. Differential effects of MSC exosomes on HPV16 and HPV18 cell lines were recorded but not linked to HPV genotype. HPV oncogenic activity is an unmeasured and plausible modifier of MSC activity in cervical cancer. Stratification by HPV oncogenic status should be a methodological requirement for interpretable and translatable evidence, because E6/E7 signalling is linked to PDL-1, TGF-β, STAT-3 and NF-κB, all linked to MSC immunomodulatory pathways. A predictive stratification system and minimum reporting standards are suggested.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review evaluates the immunological effects of mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs) in HPV-driven cervical cancer. It highlights the contradictory findings in the literature regarding MSCs' role in tumor suppression or promotion. The review identifies a critical gap in understanding the mechanisms behind these paradoxes and emphasizes the need for HPV stratification in future studies. It suggests that HPV oncogenic activity, particularly through E6/E7 signaling, influences MSC behavior and that stratification by HPV status is essential for generating interpretable and translatable evidence. The review also proposes a predictive stratification model and minimum reporting standards to improve the quality and relevance of future research.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 每年有超过 660,000 名女性患有 宫颈癌,这是由高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 持续感染引起的。本综述旨在评估 HPV 相关 宫颈癌 中 MSC 介导的免疫逃避,量化文献中的 HPV 分层失败,并制定将 MSC 行为与 HPV 致癌活性联系起来的预测分层模型。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 根据 PRISMA 2020 指南对 8 个数据库进行了系统评价。已发表的间充质干细胞/基质细胞(MSC)作为免疫调节剂的研究是相互矛盾的,一些报告抑制肿瘤,另一些报告促进肿瘤。如果研究报告 MSC 干预 宫颈癌 并产生一种或多种免疫相关结果,则研究被纳入。HPV 分层差距分析与数据提取和偏倚风险评估一起进行。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: MSC 的作用包括通过腺苷、IL-10 和 M2 巨噬细胞极化进行免疫逃避,以及通过 STAT3、Wnt/β-Catenin 和表观遗传途径抑制肿瘤。HPV 致癌活性是 宫颈癌 中 MSC 活性的未测量且合理的修饰因子。建议采用预测分层系统和最低报告标准。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 这些悖论的机制尚未得到系统研究。在 13 项已完成的研究中,没有一项研究将 HPV 致癌活性作为实验变量进行测量。记录了 MSC 外泌体对 HPV16 和 HPV18 细胞系的不同影响,但与 HPV 基因型无关。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 按 HPV 致癌状态进行分层应该是可解释和可翻译证据的方法学要求,因为 E6/E7 信号传导与 PDL-1、TGF-β、STAT-3 和 NF-κB 相关,所有这些都与 MSC 免疫调节途径相关。
